title: Hardcore Ender Dragon
description: Datapack that makes the Ender Dragon significantly harder with new attacks and behaviors.
body:
Hardcore Ender Dragon or Hardcore Dragon for short is in BETA.

This datapack make the Ender Dragon significantly harder while keeping the fight relatively vanilla. New attacks and behavior have been added to make the final boss an actual challenge unlike the vanilla one.

It's compatible with any map and custom Ender Crystals placement (the ones with a bottom part), as the place where the dragon is spawned doesn't matter. It's also in theory compatible with multiple dragons spawned simultaneously, but it may be a bit buggy if they are all at the same place in the world.

**Make sure the gamerule _doDaylightCycle_ is set to _true_.**

![Hardcore Dragon preview](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/28hT4Jxf/images/1a54549419e93ad699617feb8578204cda762420.jpeg)

### How does the fight work (simple, spoiler free):

<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

The dragon has 5 phases and they will activate as his health gets lower and lower. The first phase is just the normal dragon, and it ends when (spoiler):
<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>
all crystals are destroyed.
</details>



</details>

### How does the fight work (detailed, SPOILERS):

<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

All of the phased are additive which means in the final phase the dragon will be able to use any of the attacks of previous phases.

**Phase 0:**
- The Dragon is the vanilla one but the crystals are respawning after some time if they are not all destroyed simulteniously.

**Phase 1:**
- The Dragon gets 2 new random attacks:
  - He can summon a crystal on the head of an enderman. This enderman will follow the dragon to heal him.
  - He can charge at you.

**Phase 2:**
- The Dragon gets 1 new random attack, he can rise into the sky and create clouds that will cause many light strikes bellow them.
- The Dragon gets 1 modified attack, dragon fire balls are now repeatedly shot and are explosive.

**Phase 3:**
- The Dragon gets 2 new random attack:
  - He can breath purple "fire" everywhere he goes for a certain amount of time.
  - He can randomly decide to grab players on his way after he is done perching. You can try escaping by repetitively Sneaking. 
- The Dragon gets 2 modified attacks:
  - When he perches, he will command the endermans to attack you until he is done.
  - When he charges at you, he will be faster and can follow up with a grab.

**Phase 4:**
- The dragon stop loosing hp after a certain threshold until he start a unique new attack that will respawn the crystals you previously destroyed. This is the first thing he will try to do after entering phase 4.
- The Dragon gets 2 modified attacks:
  - When he perches, he will also spawn shulker bullets around him.
  - When he spawns an ender crystal on an enderman he will also create himself a certain amount of shield layers depending of how much players are near him. Those shields protect him from projectiles and can be destroyed with 3 shots each or in 1 shot with a trident.

**Finally:**
- The dragon go back to its perch position, rise in the sky and create a meteor. It will fall back down and make all entities take serious damage as well as launching them in the sky. After this the dragon only need one hit to be defeated. 
</details>

### Reward:

<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

After defeating the dragon, you get a Hardcore Dragon Head which, when worn, extends your range by 2 blocks.

</details>

_Contact me on [Discord](https://discordapp.com/users/316614934618439681) if you have feedback or suggestion to make or want to report a bug._

title: Ender Lead
description: A simple tool to move an entity.
body:
📦 Ender Lead
Ender Lead is a lightweight utility mod for Minecraft that adds a single, powerful item: the Ender Lead — inspired by the version found in Apotheosis, but implemented as a standalone, minimal mod.

✨ Features
Adds a new item: Ender Lead, which allows players to capture and store any entity (not just animals) and release them later.
Capture Mechanics:
Left-clicking an entity with the Ender Lead will store that entity inside the item.
Works on almost all entities, including mobs, villagers, modded creatures, etc.
When an entity is captured, it is removed from the world and saved in the item's NBT data.
Release Mechanics:
Right-clicking a block with a stored entity will spawn it at the clicked position.
Each release consumes 1 durability point (max durability: 15 uses).
Additional Features:
The item's tooltip dynamically displays the name of the stored entity.
The item glows when it contains an entity (foil effect).
Plays Enderman teleport sound when capturing or releasing an entity.
🛠️ Crafting Recipe
The Ender Lead is crafted shapelessly with:

1 × Lead

1 × Ender Pearl

1 × Gold Ingot

🎮 Gameplay Impact
The Ender Lead offers a new way to interact with entities, significantly improving entity transportation and management:

Easily move villagers, pets, bosses, or rare mobs across dimensions or long distances.

Build complex farms or bases with precise entity placement.

Capture mobs on exploration trips and release them at your base.

No need for minecarts, boats, or leads for moving mobs anymore.

It’s especially useful for technical and survival modpacks where controlling entity positions is critical.

🔍 Design Philosophy
This mod is designed to be:

Clean: Only adds a single item.

Standalone: No dependencies on other mods (like Apotheosis).

Lightweight: Ideal for performance-conscious players and modpacks.

🙏 Credits
This mod is inspired by the Ender Lead from Apotheosis, but implemented as a minimal and standalone version with the same core idea.

title: Enchantable ShulkerBox
description: This mod adds an enchantment that can be applied to the shulker box.
body:
# Enchantable Shulker Box Mod

The **Enchantable Shulker Box Mod** introduces an exciting new feature to your Minecraft world: the ability to enchant Shulker Boxes! This mod enhances the functionality of Shulker Boxes by allowing players to imbue them with powerful enchantments, starting with the **Refill** enchantment.

## Features

### 🪄 Enchantable Shulker Boxes
- Shulker Boxes can now be enchanted like regular tools and weapons.
- Enchant them through the Enchantment Table or combine enchantments with Anvils.

### ⚡ Refill Enchantment
- The **Refill** enchantment is a utility enchantment for players who love efficiency and organization.
- When you use an item (e.g., arrows, potions, or blocks) and your inventory runs out, the enchanted Shulker Box will automatically refill your inventory from its stored items.
- Perfect for builders, adventurers, and combat enthusiasts who rely on keeping their inventory well-stocked.

### 🔄 Seamless Integration
- Enchanted Shulker Boxes retain their enchantments even when broken and placed again, ensuring you never lose your enhancements.
- Fully compatible with existing enchantment mechanics, including Anvils and the Grindstone.

## Compatibility
- Works seamlessly in both single-player and multiplayer environments.
- Designed to integrate with other mods, maintaining a vanilla-friendly experience.

## Notes
- This mod currently focuses on the **Refill** enchantment but is designed to be expanded with more enchantments in the future.
- Please report any bugs or suggestions on the [issue tracker](#).

Take your storage and utility game to the next level with the **Enchantable Shulker Box Mod**!

title: DiscordLoom
description: Create a direct link between your Minecraft and Discord servers with DiscordLoomConnect, ensuring only whitelisted players have access.
body:
DiscordLoom is a mod designed to merge the diverse functionalities of Discord with the Minecraft server whitelist, enhancing the efficiency of administrative actions.

The main focus of DiscordLoom is to facilitate efficient integration of the gaming and communication platforms, ensuring that only authorized, whitelisted players can access the server, hence providing a secure and cooperative gameplay environment.

## Key Features 

- **Discord Role Synchronization:** This mod allows for the automatic syncing of roles between Discord and LuckPerms. For instance, if a player is promoted to a new role on Discord, they will also receive this new role in LuckPerms.

- **Mandatory Voice Channel:** DiscordLoom also features a mandatory voice channel requirement, ensuring that all whitelisted players are also part of the voice chat in Discord which further promotes cooperation and communication.

- **In-Game Link Process:** All necessary linking processes are integrated in-game, making it easy for players to connect their Discord accounts with their respective Minecraft server accounts.

- **Ban sync:** Minecraft banned players get banned also on discord. BanHammer is also supported

In the future, it will also link the Discord chat to offer a more immersing experience.

**Required Mods**

- [SERVER] LuckPerms: for the enhanced functionality of permissions management. 

Experience a whole new gaming environment with DiscordLoomConnect, where communication and gameplay overlap for a better gaming experience.

title: Stronghold Finder
description: Small mod for searching strongholds by two throws
body:
Mod adds clientside /eyethrow command

Usage guide:

  1. Throw eye and point camera on it
  2. run /eyethrow register, it will print id of throw
  3. Walk away from first throw 100-200 blocks
  4. Repeat steps 1 and 2
  5. run /eyethrow calculate throwid1 throwid2.

Mod will print approximate coordinates of stronghold.

Mod works similar way to ninjabrain bot, but uses only intersection of two throws in calculation, so it is not so accurate.

title: Black Ether
description: A simple mod that adds a new ore type, along with new weapons, armor and a few extra items. The new ore is called Onyx (like the gem) which can be created by smelting a diamond in the furnace. There is also a new fuel type called ether.
body:
# Black Ether Minecraft Mod
[![CodeQL](https://github.com/javachaos/blackether/actions/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/javachaos/blackether/actions/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml)

To install, go to https://modrinth.com/mod/black-ether

## Current Items:

- **Ether ore:** Burnable, lasts a little longer than coal ore. Ether is found at level 8 or lower, most commonly between 0 and 8, in vein sizes of about 5.
- **Block of ether:** Non-burnable, but can be placed into a blast furnace to create diamonds.
- **Onyx ore:** An ore slightly more valuable than diamond. Can be used to craft an Onyx Pickaxe. To create Onyx ore, simply place a diamond into either a blast furnace or a furnace and burn it to produce Onyx.
- **Onyx Pickaxe**
- **Onyx Shovel**
- **Onyx Axe**
- **Onyx Hoe**
- **Onyx Dust:** Craftable using the stonesaw. (WIP, will add more to this later. Dust is currently useless.)
- **Onyx Armor:** Craftable using onyx ore.
- **Onyx fort:** Structures which spawn randomly 1 in every 1000 chunks, filled with loot and a few goodies.
- **Onyx Snake Mob:** An onyx snake which has a few animations and is hostile. Spawns in forests at night, as well as in the deep dark.

*This mod changes how diamonds can be acquired. A new recipe was introduced to allow the player to smelt a block of ether or place a block of ether into the blast furnace to create a diamond. Cooking time in the blast furnace is 3x as fast.*

### **Requires:**

- **Geckolib:** *1.19.4:4.1.0*
- **Fabric Loader:** *0.14.17*
- **Minecraft:** *1.19.4*

title: ProxyPortal
description: Build portals on a Fabric server to teleport between servers via Velocity.
body:
# ProxyPortal

ProxyPortal is a mod designed for Fabric servers that uses Velocity as a proxy server, allowing admins to create portals for quickly teleporting between different servers. **Portals are invisible regions and do not generate any blocks or structures automatically.** Admins need to decorate portals with blocks, lights, or particle effects to make them visually recognizable to players.

## Requirements

**Proxy Server**: Velocity (for cross-server functionality)

## Features

**Custom Portals**: Create portals to teleport players between servers.

**Native Portal Override**: Automatically cancels native teleportation for Nether Portals, End Portals, and End Gateways.

## Usage

### Permission Requirements

All ProxyPortal commands require **administrator permissions** (permission level 2 or above).

### Create Portal
```
/portal create <name> <x1> <y1> <z1> <x2> <y2> <z2> <target_server>
```

- `<name>`: Unique name for the portal
- `<x1> <y1> <z1>`: First corner coordinates of the portal area
- `<x2> <y2> <z2>`: Second corner coordinates of the portal area
- `<target_server>`: Target server name (as configured in Velocity)

**Example:**
```
/portal create spawn_portal 100 64 200 105 70 205 lobby
```
This creates a portal named "spawn_portal" with area from coordinates (100,64,200) to (105,70,205), targeting the "lobby" server.

### Delete Portal
```
/portal delete <name>
```

### List All Portals
```
/portal list
```

### Reload Portal Data
```
/portal reload
```

title: Sketchy Books
description: Sketchy Books lets you draw pixel-art sketches directly inside Books & Quills, turning them into illustrated journals.
body:
**Sketchy Books** lets you draw pixel-art sketches directly inside **Books & Quills**, turning them into true illustrated journals.

Before signing a book, players can freely doodle on its pages using a simple pixel-based drawing interface, allowing sketches, symbols, diagrams, or small drawings to be added alongside written text.

Once the book is signed, all drawings and text are permanently preserved inside the signed book, just like vanilla content. Illustrated books can then be shared, traded, or stored without losing any data.

The mod is fully **server-compatible** and works seamlessly in **multiplayer**, ensuring that all players see the same drawings exactly as intended.

Sketchy Books is designed as a lightweight, vanilla-friendly quality-of-life mod that expands the creative and practical use of books without altering core gameplay.

title: Zombies Improve Over Time
description: Zombies get stronger the longer you play. Buffs include increasing health, damage, knockback resistance, etc.
body:
# Zombies Improve Over Time
This datapack increases zombies's stats over time. The changes are made to be gradual, increasing very slightly each minecraft day up to day 100. Difficulty is calculated for each player separately. New players will start with weak zombies while players who have been playing for a while will have stronger zombies.

## NOTICE: This datapack is discontinued, instead use the Hostile Mobs Improve Over Time datapack: https://modrinth.com/datapack/hostile-mobs-improve-over-time 

### Stat increase
Stats that change include:
- Health
- Damage
- Reinforcement chance
- Knockback resistance
- Movement speed
- Armor and armor toughness

Day 50 enables all zombies to break doors\
Day 70~ - enables all zombies to pick up loot\
Day 80 - some zombies change to baby/or have leather armor\
Day 95 - Zombies might gain strenght and speed when near player\
some other stuff

### Commands
If you wish to test out how hard the zombies are, use functions diff:day25, diff:day50, diff:day75, diff:100 or use command "scoreboard players set <player> Timeroo <number> . To reset your score use diff:reset, or diff:resetall to reset all of players difficulty. 
### Timers
Timer for difficulty is per player, and increases every minecraft day (20 minutes). sleeping does NOT forward this timer. Max difficulty is day 100+ and difficulty does not increase after that.
### Installing
like your ordinary datapack, put zip file in your datapacks folder of your world
### Unistalling
use function diff:unistall and then remove your datapack from your datapacks folder
### Other
I am planning on making a version of this datapack for each common mob, then making a datapack consisting of all of them

[![Button](https://i.imgur.com/197JTrg.png)](https://server.pro/?ref=JustTimmsAdditions "Sponsored by Server.pro") --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ### We are rebranding this resource pack, making it work without optifine or CIT Resewn and making a datapack so this resource pack works in survival without renaming. It will take a while until it's finished so if you want to keep up to date with the latest news then join our [Discord Server](https://discord.gg/runTSv2)!

Custom Additions is a Resource Pack that uses OptiFine's/CIT Resewn's Custom Item Textures *(CIT)* feature to add many item and armor textures to the game. I want to add many big updates and the resource pack also includes many collections with items based on different games, movies or series. You can find Custom Additions on [Modrinth](https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/justtimms-custom-additions) and [PlanetMinecraft](https://www.planetminecraft.com/texture-pack/justtimm-s-custom-additions/)! Items: **338**
You can find all the items in the [documentation](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1c1bp56e_AJ-xW5XDIwqWsIzhILaA5YN8/view?usp=sharing)! ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Download **OptiFine** or **CIT Resewn** for this Resource Pack to work properly. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- **Keep in mind that there are 2 versions of this Resource Pack! A Vanilla & [Vanilla Additions](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/texture-packs/justtimms-vanilla-additions) version.**
How does it work? It’s really simple. Make sure you have OptiFine installed, that the setting `Custom Items` is set to **`ON`** *(Video Settings -> Quality)* and that you have the resource pack `enabled`. If you want to get one of our custom items you need to get yourself an anvil and the required item. ***Example**: I want to get a pear. In order to get it I need to place an apple in the first slot and then change the name of it. It’s possible that some items require an enchantment. Then you need to put the right enchantment book in the middle slot.*

title: Origins: Tiltkin
description: An alcohol brewing themed Origin for the Origins Mod. Tiltkin are more than mere brewers; they are crooked caretakers of The Tilted Tavern, a lopsided pocket of reality where the ale is strong and the shadows stronger.
body:
<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/VQHmx_fHSM0" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe>
<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/k6S3zzWImxg" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe>

**This data pack is designed for the Origins mod.**

[This Origin was suggested by **uzunuro** on Discord. If you would like to suggest your own data pack, you can do so over on my Discord server as well.](https://discord.gg/b8jJUQ29Wg)

**Tiltkin:** Tiltkin are more than mere brewers; they are crooked caretakers of The Tilted Tavern, a lopsided pocket of reality where the ale is strong and the shadows stronger. Their domain is a place of slanted hearths and tilted morals, where every mug runneth over; sometimes with things that shouldn’t be drunk. The air hums with half-remembered drinking songs, and the chandelier sways to a wind that doesn’t exist.

**Impact:** 🟢

**🟩 The Grinning Threshold [Primary]:** You open the Grinning Threshold, its hinges stretching like a cat’s yawn, and step into your Tilted Tavern, dragging those nearby along with you. The floor greets you with a familiar slant, the firelight flickering in ways that defy geometry.

**🟩 Last Call [Primary + Sneak]:** With a resonant clunk, the Tavern firmly escorts all patrons out. Those who resist find their legs moving on their own, stepping through the door as if carried by an unseen tide.

**🟩 Tiltkin’s Keg [Secondary + Sneak]:** A Tiltkin’s Keg seeps from the darkness, its wooden ribs creaking like a waking beast. The Tiltkin’s Keg, as the name implies, is your brewing crucible; check your advancements to see what brews you can concoct.

**🟢 Iron Liver:** Poisons? Mere seasoning. Curses? They glide off you like rainwater. Your blood is half-distilled already, and your veins hum with the Tavern’s defiance.

**🟢 Swift as a Pouring Tap:** You move with the liquid ease of a spilled drink, the very air parting for you like patrons before a brawl. Stairs tilt to meet your feet, and doors creak open just in time.

**🟢 Tavern’s Warmth:** The hearth’s glow mends wounds and soothes aches; though those who linger too long start forgetting why you would ever leave.

**🟡 The Walls Have Teeth:** The Tavern tolerates no violence. Blades dull mid-swing, spells fizzle like damp fuses, and those who strike the bar find their hands stuck fast to the wood. The shadows bite back.

**🔴 The Coven’s Tab:** Brew past midnight, and the hagged patrons you’ve stolen clients from send their debt collectors: ghostly cats with eyes like frozen lanterns. You cannot blink, cannot brew, and can barely even look away until they’re... dealt with, yowling back into the dark.

**🔴 The Host’s Hands:** Your fingers were made for pouring, not punching. Your strikes land as softly as a cork dropped in sawdust; though the Tavern might lend a hand if you’re clever with a bottle.

**🔴 The Vanishing Latch:** After taking damage, the Threshold hiccups shut for 15 seconds. It’ll return, once it’s finished laughing at you.


<details>
<summary>🍺 Alcohol System Framework 🍺</summary>

Players can have up to three different alcohols active at once.
- The level of drunkenness depends on how many alcohols are currently active.
- Drinking a fourth alcohol is blocked.
- Attempting to drink a duplicate of an already active alcohol is also blocked.

Sobering up from any level of drunkenness will trigger a hangover.
- Sleeping automatically clears all active alcohols and immediately causes a hangover.

Drinking milk removes all drunkenness and even cures hangovers, but at a cost:
- It will apply the "Sour Stomach" debuff, inducing hunger for 15 seconds.

# Tipsy
**Description:** The world sways like a drunkard’s lullaby.

**🟡 Honeyed Haze:** Pale gold bubbles escape your lips; harmless, but marking you as the Tavern’s guest.

**🟡 The Telltale Hiccup:** A faint hiccup betrays you in the silence.

**🔴 Slanted Sight:** The edges of your vision ripple, as if reflected in a disturbed ale.

**🔴 The Floor’s Whisper:** Your footing drifts slightly, as though the ground sways beneath you.

# Drunk
**Description:** Reality is just a suggestion you agreed to earlier.

**🟡 Cinder’s Whisper:** Frequent orange-red bubbles trail your lips, glowing like dying coals.

**🟡 Bartender’s Interruption:** Your speech breaks into frequent, echoing hiccups.

**🔴 The Hearth’s Gaze:** The world bends like wax near a flame; edges warp, doors stretch unnaturally.

**🔴 The Sailor’s Shame:** Your footing slips a storm-tossed ship; movement gains unpredictable momentum.

# Blackout
**Description:** The Tavern sings, and you’re just the instrument.

**🟡 The Drunkard’s Chorus:** Hiccups wrack your body near-constantly, each one echoing like a misplayed note. 

**🟡 The Hag’s Sigh:** Your breath spills a swirling purple-pink mist, thick as stolen wine.

**🔴 Butterfingers:** A 5% chance to fumble items when used, as if the Tavern itself plucks at them.

**🔴 Jester’s Leading Step:** Your body lurches violently, as if the floor tilts by whim. 

**🔴 The Backwards Waltz:** Your limbs rebel; left is right, forward is backward. 

**🔴 The Curtain’s Fall:** Your vision cuts out without warning, plunging you into momentary darkness. 

**🔴 The Melted Chandelier:** Reality drips like tallow, walls slumping into impossible shapes. 

# Hungover
**Description:** The Tavern always collects its due; in memories, or in pounding regret.

**🔴 Molasses Marrow:** Your limbs move through thick air, each step an effort.

**🔴 The Coven's Tax:** Your body rebels, your vitality lowered, as if something vital was drunk in your stead.

**🔴 The Sun's Mockery:** Daylight becomes agony, a searing white shroud over your vision in bright light.

</details>


<details>
<summary>🍺 Alcohols 🍺</summary>

# Apple Cider
## Recipe:
A sun-blessed brew, crisp as an autumn morn and sweet as a bard’s love song. Favored by weary travelers and merry villagers alike, its golden hue whispers of ripened apples out in the fields.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Toss in a plump **Apple**, plucked at the peak of juiciness.
- Stir in a pinch of **Sugar** to rouse the sleeping yeasts.
- Finish with a bundle of golden **Wheat**, lending it the heartiness of a harvest feast.
## Effects:
**🟢 Golden Heart:** Gain +2 armor points while holding food of the harvest; it’s warmth strengthening you.

**🟢 Harvest’s Bounty:** Eating food restores +2 extra hunger points and grants +20% movement speed for 30 seconds.

**🟢 Sun-Kissed Vigor:** Passive health regen while under sunlight. The cider carries the warmth of an autumn sun.

**🔴 Sweet Scent:** Bees are drawn to you and may sting, even if unprovoked. The cider’s sweetness lingers on your skin.

# Cactus Tequila
## Recipe:
A scorching amber spirit that dances on the tongue like desert wind over dunes. Caravanners and foolhardy adventurers toast with it, laughing as their lips tingle with ember-sweet rebellion.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Chop in a **Cactus**, its flesh bitter as a bandit’s pride and twice as sharp.
- Stir in a pinch of **Blaze Powder**, stolen from the heart of a Nether ember, to ignite the soul.
- Sweeten with **Sugar**, a golden kiss to tame the flame, lest it burns more than just the tongue.
## Effects:
**🟢 Bandit’s Defiance:** Melee hits after drinking deal +2 extra damage and briefly ignites the target. 

**🟢 Dune Strider:** Movement speed +50% in hot biomes. The desert’s harshness fuels your stride.

**🟡 Prickly Aura:** Passively damage all those nearby. The cactus’s spines don’t discriminate.

# Carrot Wine
## Recipe:
A deceptively noble taste, with earthy sweetness and a luminous glow that dances in the glass like liquid sunset. Beloved by both tipsy tavern-goers and discerning rabbits with a taste for the finer things.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Toss in a **Carrot**, scrubbed clean of the soil’s embrace, its sweetness waiting to awaken.
- Stir in a pinch of **Sugar**, to coax out its hidden nectar and sweeten the deal.
- Finish with a sprinkle of **Glowstone Dust**, igniting the brew with a golden shimmer; as if capturing the last rays of dusk.
## Effects:
**🟢 Earthen Resilience:** Armor toughness +1 when standing on dirt, grass, or farmland. The carrot’s roots tie you to the earth.

**🟢 Luminous Sight:** Gain sight in the dark; the essence of the glowstone improving your sight.

**🟢 Rabbit’s Grace:** Jump higher, +1 blocks, and experience fall damage reduced by 1 heart. The wine carries the lightness of a hare’s leap.

**🔴 Hollowburrow Hunger:** The spirit of the rabbit now burns through you. It eats what you eat, and then some.

# Chorus Fruit Liqueur
## Recipe:
A volatile elixir that dances on the tongue like starlight; one sip may send your spirit soaring or leave you stranded in a haze of regret. Beloved by reckless adventurers and foolhardy sorcerers who dare to gamble with fate.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Crush a **Popped Chorus Fruit**, its fractured whispers fizzing with unstable magic.
- Stir in a heap of **Sugar**, to sweeten the deal... or disguise the danger.
- Drop in an **Ender Pearl**, its dimensional energies infusing the brew with an unsettling but addictive vibration.
## Effects:
**🟢 Chorus Resonance:** Melee attacks chain to 1 nearby enemy. The liqueur sings when you fight.

**🟢 Echoing Evasion:** 10% chance for damage to phase through you harmlessly. Reality glitches around you.

**🟢 Fractured Momentum:** Every 10 seconds, you will teleport to the block you are currently looking at. The liqueur’s magic refuses to let you stand still.

**🔴 The Watchers:** Endermen are drawn to you, instinctively attacking you without being provoked. They know you’ve been tampering.

# Dandelion Gin
## Recipe:
A mischievous elixir, its floral bouquet dances on the tongue before a slow, creeping warmth reminds you that some beauties bite back. Favored by rogue alchemists and those who like their drinks with a whisper of danger.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Pluck a **Dandelion**, sun-drunk and puffing with pollen, and drop it in without a second thought.
- Add a **Spider Eye**, glistening with venomous charm, for a medicinal aftertaste that lingers like a whispered secret.
- **Sugar** to mask the bite, a generous pour, like bribing a trickster spirit.
## Effects:
**🟢 Pollen’s Grace:** Jump higher, +1 blocks, and experience fall damage reduced by 1 heart. The dandelion’s lightness lingers in your bones.

**🟢 Solar Flare:** When hit below half health, release a burst of light, blinding nearby enemies for 2 seconds. The dandelion remembers the sun’s wrath.

**🟢 Venom’s Kiss:** Your melee attacks poison enemies for 3 seconds. The spider’s bite hides in every sip.

**🔴 Insect’s Grudge:** Silverfish and spiders deal increased damage to you. The spider eye in the gin calls its kin.

# Dragon’s Breath Brandy
## Recipe:
A scorching elixir that dances on the tongue like a wyrm’s last laugh; this molten amber spirit is liquid courage with teeth. Only foolish adventurers dare sip it, for its embered aftertaste lingers long after the bottle’s empty.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Toss in a splash of **Dragon’s Breath**, stolen from the maw of The End’s great beast.
- Stir in a heap of **Sugar**, a desperate plea to spare your throat from cinders.
- Finish with a **Nether Wart**, its cursed roots weaving the flames into something barely drinkable.
## Effects:
**🟢 Cinder Tongue:** Spit out a constant stream of flames whilst sneaking. The brandy fights its way back out.

**🟢 Scorched Hide:** Fire damage has no impact on you. Your blood burns too hot to be harmed.

**🟢 Wyrm’s Heart:** Your fists and melee weapons ignite enemies for 3 seconds. The brandy’s fire lives in your veins.

**🔴 Thirst of the Pyre:** Water contact deals significant damage. Your body rejects moisture.

# Ghastly Gin
## Recipe:
A spirit as pale as a wraith’s sigh, distilled from tears. Hauntingly smooth, it leaves a chill like a specter’s touch; favored by heartbroken poets, reckless adventurers, and those who laugh a little too loudly in empty taverns.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Drop in a **Ghast Tear**, shimmering with the sorrow of the Nether’s lost souls.
- Stir in a pinch of **Sugar**, a fleeting attempt to sweeten the bitterness of fate.
- Finish with a **Fermented Spider Eye**, its murky depths swirling with lingering regret.
## Effects:
**🟢 Chill of the Departed:** Gain immunity to fire, your skin grows cold to the touch. The Nether’s sorrows dampen flames.

**🟢 Wraith’s Whisper:** 10% chance for damage to phase through you harmlessly. The gin’s spectral nature lets you flicker like a ghost.

# Gilded Absinthe
## Recipe:
The drink of poets and fools; one sip, and the world unravels in emerald dreams. A shimmering, venomous green elixir that dances between delirium and delight, cherished by mad artists and those who dare to peer beyond the veil.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Drop in a **Golden Apple**, its gilded skin hiding nectar fit for kings.
- Stir in a pinch of **Sugar**, a stolen spark of sweetness to lure the unwary.
- Finish with a **Fermented Spider Eye**, its cursed tang twisting the brew into something wicked and wonderful.
## Effects:
**🟢 Ambrosial Sip:** Eating food restores +4 extra hunger points and grants absorption.

**🟢 Gilded Resilience:** Gain +10 health. The gold in your veins hardens against fate.

**🟢 Sun-Kissed Flesh:** Gain health regeneration when entering sunlight. The apple’s divine energy lingers.

**🔴 Midas’ Folly:** Your gilded flesh stills your movement, moving 25% slower. The gilding is unstable.

# Glow Berry Champagne
## Recipe:
A mischievous brew that sparkles like starlight caught in a glass. Its radiant bubbles dance with every sip, leaving a faint luminescence on the lips, perfect for toasting triumphs. Favored by adventurers who laugh in the face of danger.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Crush **Glow Berries** into the keg, their bioluminescent juices swirling like captured fairy lights.
- Stir in **Sugar**, coaxing the mixture into a frenzy of sweet, shimmering bubbles.
- Finish with a dash of **Gunpowder**, because why settle for fizz when you can have fireworks on the tongue?
## Effects:
**🟢 Firework Blood:** Taking damage causes a burst of colored sparks, briefly blinding attackers. Your veins run with celebratory defiance.

**🟢 Starlight Sip:** Gain sight in the dark. The champagne’s glow illuminating the dark.

**🟡 Firework Belly:** Release explosions over time, harmless to you, but hurting those around you. The gunpowder remembers its purpose.

# Honey Mead
## Recipe:
The nectar of the gods, if gods were tipsy bees. Golden and ambrosial, this drink hums with the lazy warmth of a midsummer hive. Beloved by bards, beekeepers, and those who fancy themselves part of a very drunk pantheon.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Pour in a **Honey Bottle**, its contents stolen from a hive drowsy with sunlight.
- Stir in a pinch of **Sugar**, a spark of mortal greed to out-sweeten nature itself.
- Toss in a proud stalk of **Wheat**, for a rustic whisper of the harvest’s embrace.
## Effects:
**🟢 Ambrosial Aura:** Nearby allies gain regeneration while standing close to you. The mead’s golden warmth radiates like a beehive’s hum.

**🟢 Hive’s Blessing:** Bees ignore you as they falsely recognize you as one of their own.

**🟢 Honeyed Words:** Villagers offer better trades. The mead’s sweetness makes you charming.

**🔴 Honeyed Sloth:** You find yourself unable to sprint. The mead’s drowsy warmth makes haste feel vulgar.

# Magma Mead
## Recipe:
This searing concoction bubbles like molten rock and burns with the fury of the Nether itself. Only the foolhardy, or those with fireproof gullets, dare take a sip. Its amber glow pulses like embers, and the aftertaste lingers like a dragon’s breath.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Stir in a glob of **Magma Cream**, its viscous fire begging to be unleashed.
- Toss in a heap of **Sugar**, a fleeting illusion of sweetness before the inferno claims your tongue.
- Finish with **Blaze Powder**, ensuring each sip burns twice, once going down, and once in your guts.
## Effects:
**🟢 Molten Momentum:** Movement speed +50%. The ground remembers your passing.

**🟢 Netherforged Skin:** Gain immunity to fire. Your veins run with liquid embers.

**🟢 Scorched Presence:** Mobs that you touch or touch you ignite. The mead’s fury seeps from your pores.

**🔴 Nether’s Claim:** If you die while the mead is active, your corpse explodes. The Nether reclaims its gifts violently.

# Nether Wart Rum
## Recipe:
A devil’s draught, dark as a soul forfeit and spiced like a smuggler’s last confession. Pirates weep for this recipe, not from sorrow, but from the fire that lingers long after the bottle’s drained. Only the reckless or the doomed dare drink it.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Toss in a fistful of **Nether Wart**, plucked from the ashen soil where shadows whisper.
- Stir in a heap of **Sugar**, a coward’s attempt to mask the sin before it sears your throat.
- Finish with **Blaze Powder**, because hell should burn twice, and so should you.
## Effects:
**🟢 Blighted Strikes:** Melee attacks apply withering to non-undead enemies. Your blows carry the fortress’s rot.

**🟢 Fortress Scent:** Creatures of the Nether Fortress ignore you presence unless provoked. You reek of netherwart and ash, they mistake you for part of the ruins.

**🟢 Wither’s Endurance:** Gain +10 health while in the Nether. The fortress’s curse lends you its stubborn defiance.

**🔴 Hollowing:** Take damage over time when outside the Nether. The rum’s power fades, leaving your body to crumble like netherrack.

# Phantom Gin
## Recipe:
Bottled insomnia. One sip, and you’ll never sleep again. This pale, ghostly spirit flickers like a dying lantern, its taste sharp as a specter’s whisper. Favored by thieves, scholars burning midnight oil, and fools who dare to outwit the dawn.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Fold in a **Phantom Membrane**, harvested fresh from the clutches of nightmares.
- Stir in a pinch of **Sugar**, to sweeten the terrors lurking within.
- Drop in a **Fermented Spider Eye**, for fear is bitter.
## Effects:
**🟢 Phantom’s Gaze:** Gain sight in the dark; the eyes of the phantom becoming yours.

**🟢 Phantom’s Grace:** Movement speed +50% at night. The restless dead lend you their haste.

**🟢Specter’s Grasp:** Melee strikes inflict levitation; your blows carry the weightless dread of the night, sending foes drifting upward like lost spirits.

**🔴 Sleepless Debt:** You cannot sleep in beds. The Tavern claims your rest as payment.

# Potato Vodka
## Recipe:
Clear as a mountain glacier and strong enough to knock a giant off its feet. This unpretentious spirit is the liquid courage of miners, mercenaries, and those who’d rather forget their troubles.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Toss in a stout **Potato**, rugged and unpeeled, as rough-handed as the miners who prize it.
- Stir in a pinch of **Sugar**, a sly thief’s trick to smooth the edge off a thief’s regret.
- Finish with a proud stalk of **Wheat**, lending a whisper of golden fields to the otherwise unrepentant burn.
## Effects:
**🟢 Glacial Numbness:** Take 30% less damage from all sources. The vodka dulls pain as easily as it dulls regrets.

**🟢 Miner’s Resolve:** Mining speed increases by 50%. The spirit of stubborn toil lingers in every sip.

**🟢 Swing First, Think Never:** Melee attacks deal +4 damage. Your drunken stupor increases your strength.

**🔴 Reversal:** Upon killing an enemy, you will take damage. The Tavern collects its debt in blood.

# Pufferfish Punch
## Recipe:
A drink as daring as a pirate’s last gamble, its venomous bite tempered into a tingling thrill. Only the foolhardy or the truly desperate dare to sip, but those who survive swear it grants visions of the ocean’s deepest secrets. Favored by rogue alchemists and thrill-seeking sailors.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Toss in a **Pufferfish**, its spines still whispering of the reef’s deadly embrace.
- Stir in a pinch of **Sugar**, a sweet lie to soothe the creeping numbness.
- Finish with a **Slimeball**, its ooze thickening the brew into something dubiously drinkable.
## Effects:
**🟢 Nimble Float:** Jump higher, +1 blocks, and experience fall damage reduced by 1 heart. 

**🟢 Venom’s Kiss:** Melee attacks poison enemies for 3 seconds. The punch’s toxins linger in your blood.

**🟢 Water Adaptation:** Breath in water as easily as you would in air. The gills of the pufferfish infusing oxygen into you.

**🔴 Toxin Tremors:** Burn through your hunger faster, requiring more food intake. Your stomach fights the lingering poison.

# Pumpkin Spice Liqueur
## Recipe:
Autumn in a bottle, swirling with the warmth of crackling hearths and whispered incantations. Its golden-amber glow holds the essence of fallen leaves and candlelit covens. Beloved by witches and pumpkin-patch wanderers alike.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Drop in a **Carved Pumpkin**, its flesh scooped bare to better steep its earthy sweetness.
- Stir in a heap of **Sugar**, like a coven’s blessing to tempt the tongue.
- Finish with a humble **Stick**, charmed near enough to cinnamon to fool the senses.
## Effects:
**🟢 Moonlit Brew:** Movement speed +50% at night. The coven’s magic stirs under moonlight.

**🟢 Moonlit Vigor:** Melee damage +50% at night. The witches smile as their brew fuels your violence.

**🟢 Spiced Blood:** Gain immunity to fire; the spices in your veins gently increasing your heat tolerance.

**🔴 Sugar Crash:** Burn through your hunger faster, requiring more food intake. The sweetness fades, leaving you emptier than before.

# Redstone Rum
## Recipe:
A volatile concoction that hums with raw energy, crackling on the tongue like a misfired piston. Engineers swear by its electrifying buzz, while madmen chase the phantom sparks dancing behind their eyelids. One sip, and your veins might just light up like a redstone circuit.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Stir in a pile of **Redstone Dust**, pulsing with untamed power.
- Sweeten with **Sugar**, because even lightning craves a little indulgence.
- Toss in **Glowstone Dust**, in case all of that energy wouldn’t have you glowing already.
## Effects:
**🟢 Energy Surge:** Your hunger does not drain. The rum burns calories for you.

**🟢 Overclocked Reflexes:** Break blockers 50% faster. Your muscles twitch with redstone’s rhythm.

**🟢 Overclocked Sight:** Gain sight in the dark; the essence of the glowstone improving your sight.

**🔴 Jittery Hands:** Cannot hold a steady crosshair; your fingers buzz too much for precision.

# Slimeball Shots
## Recipe:
A murky, wobbling concoction that clings to the glass, and your regrets. Its eye-watering sourness and dubious texture make it a rite of passage for reckless adventurers and masochistic alchemists. The aftertaste lingers like a curse.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Drop in a **Slimeball**, still quivering with residual malice.
- Toss in a heap of **Sugar**, a futile attempt to mask the inevitable suffering.
- Finish with a **Fermented Spider Eye**, because true despair requires depth.
## Effects:
**🟢 Skyward Strike:** Deal +20% melee damage while airborne. The slime’s residual bounce fuels your momentum.

**🟢 Slime-Launched:** Jump higher, +1 blocks, and experience fall damage reduced by 1 heart. 

**🔴 Ground Penalty:** Find yourself heavily slowed while on the ground. Your skin oozes a tar like substance, making ground movement a pain.

# Sweet Berry Wine
## Recipe:
A drink of summer love and poor life choices. Its ruby hue winks like a rogue’s promise, too sweet to resist and too bright to forget. Gulped down by starry-eyed dreamers and reckless adventurers, it leaves lips stained and memories hazier than twilight.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Crush in a handful of **Sweet Berries**, bursting with the reckless joy of sun-drunk afternoons.
- Stir in a heap of **Sugar**, to speed up tomorrow’s regret.
- Drop in a few **Glow Berries**, because even mistakes should glitter like fool’s gold.
## Effects:
**🟢 Berry-Blessed:** Eating any berry restores +4 hunger points and grants 5 seconds of +75% movement speed. The wine enhances its own tastes.

**🟢 Fool’s Glow:** Gain sight in the dark, as well as glowing. Even in darkness, your poor choices shine.

**🟢 Stolen Kiss:** Your attacks inflict weakness. The wine’s sweetness lingers like a lover’s touch.

**🔴 First Heartbreak:** Lose 4 health while active. The wine’s sweetness curdles into something hollow.

# Wheat Beer
## Recipe:
A simple, hearty brew, as reliable as a farmer’s calloused hands and as comforting as a hearthfire’s glow. Beloved by villagers and adventurers alike, its golden-amber depths carry the warmth of sunlit fields and the faint whisper of earthy fermentation.
- Begin by prepping your **Keg** with a **Bottle of Water**.
- Toss in a bundle of **Wheat**, harvested at dawn when the stalks still cling to the morning’s dew.
- Drop in a **Brown Mushroom**, its hidden spores lending a burst of wild yeast.
- Stir in a pinch of **Sugar**, just enough to rouse the drowsing fungi into a merry, bubbling dance.
## Effects:
**🟢 Earthy Resilience:** Gain +30% resistance to all damage; your body absorb damage like packed soil.

**🟢 Harvest’s Stamina:** Your hunger does not drain. The beer fuels endurance like a farmer’s steady labor.

**🟢 Village Favor:** Villagers offer better trades. They trust a fellow wheat enthusiast.

**🔴 Plowman’s Burden:** Your legs refuse to hurry, sprinting is impossible. Your legs exhausted from the fields.

</details>


[If you have any questions, concerns, or bugs you would like to report, my Discord server is a great place for doing so.](https://discord.gg/b8jJUQ29Wg)

title: AdvancedBanZ
description: AdvancedBanZ is a updated fork of the original AdvancedBan plugin by Leoko.
body:
***# Please note: This is a fork of the original AdvancedBan or AdvancedBanX plugin. Do not request support in the official AdvancedBan Discord; instead, seek help on the GitHub repository's issues page.***

### Description

AdvancedBanZ is a fork of AdvancedBanX, which itself is a modernized update of the original AdvancedBan plugin developed by Leoko. It is an all-in-one punishment system supporting warnings (warn), temporary warnings (tempwarn), mutes, temporary mutes (tempmute), bans, temporary bans (tempban), IP bans (ipban), and kicks. The plugin also provides a player history feature to view past punishment records.

The plugin supports configurable time and message templates, automatically calculating and increasing punishment durations based on specific reasons. AdvancedBanZ provides complete message files, allowing you to freely modify and translate all prompts, and includes a detailed main configuration file with numerous practical options.

Currently, AdvancedBanZ supports Bukkit (Spigot/Paper) and BungeeCord platforms, and supports both MySQL and local file storage for data persistence.

### Installation Steps

1. Download the plugin from *[Modrinth](https://modrinth.com/plugin/advancedbanz)*.
2. Place the plugin into your `plugins` folder (applicable for both Bukkit and BungeeCord).
3. Reload or restart your server.
4. Use `/advancedban` to check if the plugin loaded successfully.
5. Configure as needed and start using it.

> **Optional Tip**: If you encounter issues connecting to the database, try adjusting the MySQL version to 5.X.

### Command Reference

<details open>
<summary>View All Commands</summary>

Legend:
- `[Required] <Optional>`: `|` means "or", `-s` indicates a silent punishment (does not notify others)

- `/kick<-s> [Player] <Reason | @LayoutName>`  
  Kick a player

- `/ban /mute /warn /note <-s> [Player] <Reason | @LayoutName>`  
  Ban / Mute / Warn a player, or add a note to them

- `/banip <-s> [Player/IP] <Reason | @LayoutName>`  
  Ban a player's IP (if a player name is entered, the cached IP is used)

- `/tempban /tempmute /tempwarn <-s> [Player] [Xmo|Xd|Xh|Xm|Xs|#TimeLayout] <Reason | @LayoutName>`  
  Issue a temporary punishment with a specified duration or auto-calculated duration based on a time layout

- `/tempipban <-s> [Player/IP] [Xmo|Xd|Xh|Xm|Xs|#TimeLayout] <Reason | @LayoutName>`  
  Temporarily ban a player's IP (Alias: `/tipban`)

- `/change-reason [ID] [New Reason]`  
  Modify the reason based on the punishment ID

- `/change-reason [ban/mute] [Player] [New Reason]`  
  Modify the reason for a player's current ban or mute

- `/unban /unmute [Player]`  
  Unban or unmute a player

- `/unwarn /unnote [ID]`  
  Remove a warning or note

- `/unwarn /unnote clear [Player]`  
  Remove all warnings or notes for a player

- `/unpunish [ID]`  
  Remove any type of punishment record

- `/warns /notes <Player>`  
  View your own or another player's list of warnings/notes

- `/check [Player]`  
  Get player status: UUID / IP / Country / Ban Status / Mute Status / Warning Count / Note Count

- `/banlist <Page>`  
  View all currently active punishments

- `/history [Player] <Page>`  
  View a player's historical punishment records (requires permission `ab.history`)

- `/advancedban reload`  
  Reload message files and some settings

- `/advancedban help`  
  Display all commands and their brief descriptions

- `/systemprefs`  
  Display system information helpful for configuration
</details>

### Permission Nodes

<details open>
<summary>All Permissions</summary>

```yaml
ab.kick.use - /kick
ab.kick.exempt - Exempt from being kicked
ab.notify.kick - Receive kick notifications

ab.ban.perma - /ban
ab.ban.temp - /tempban
ab.ban.undo - /unban
ab.ban.exempt - Exempt from being banned
ab.notify.ban - Receive ban notifications
ab.undoNotify.ban - Receive unban notifications

ab.notify.tempban - Receive temporary ban notifications

ab.ipban.perma - /ipban
ab.ipban.temp - /tempipban
ab.notify.ipban - Receive IP ban notifications

ab.tempipban.exempt - Exempt from temporary IP bans
ab.notify.tempipban - Receive temporary IP ban notifications

ab.mute.perma - /mute
ab.mute.temp - /tempmute
ab.mute.undo - /unmute
ab.mute.exempt - Exempt from being muted
ab.notify.mute - Receive mute notifications
ab.undoNotify.mute - Receive unmute notifications

ab.notify.tempmute - Receive temporary mute notifications

ab.warn.perma - /warn
ab.warn.temp - /tempwarn
ab.warn.undo - /unwarn
ab.warn.exempt - Exempt from being warned
ab.notify.warn - Receive warning notifications
ab.undoNotify.warn - Receive unwarn notifications

ab.notify.tempwarn - Receive temporary warning notifications

ab.note.use - /note
ab.note.undo - /unnote
ab.note.exempt - Exempt from having notes added
ab.notify.note - Receive note notifications
ab.undoNotify.note - Receive note removal notifications

ab.all.undo - /unpunish

ab.warns.own - /warns (view self)
ab.warns.other - /warns PLAYER (view others)

ab.notes.own - /notes (view self)
ab.notes.other - /notes PLAYER (view others)

ab.check - /check
ab.check.ip - Also display IP

ab.changeReason - /change-reason
ab.banlist - /banlist
ab.history - /history
ab.reload - /advancedban reload
ab.help - /advancedban help
ab.systemprefs - /systemprefs
```
</details>

<details open>
<summary>Limiting Punishment Durations</summary>

By default, users can punish others indefinitely as long they have the corresponding permission. You can set maximum punishment durations via `ab.tempban/tempmute/tempwarn.dur.X`.

In the configuration file, there is a section named `TempPerms` that can be used to define the maximum punishment duration for different IDs. For example:

```yaml
1: 3600
```

This means a user with the permission `ab.tempban.dur.1` can only ban for a maximum of 3600 seconds (i.e., 1 hour). The unit is seconds. If a user has multiple such permissions, the one with the higher number takes precedence. See `config.yml` for more details.
</details>

<details open>
<summary>Hierarchical Exemption Permissions</summary>

For servers with large teams and complex hierarchies, you may need finer control over who can punish whom.

To do this, you can assign exemption level permissions to users in the following format:

```yaml
ab.TYPE.exempt.X
```

Where:
- `TYPE` can be: ban, tempban, ipban, tempipban, warn, tempwarn, kick, mute, tempmute
- `X` is an integer from 1 to 10 (10 is the highest privilege)

If X is not specified (i.e., just `ab.TYPE.exempt`), it is equivalent to `ab.TYPE.exempt.11`, meaning complete immunity.

> Note: Exemption permissions only take effect when the target player is online (unless using LuckPerms!)  
> Users of the same level cannot punish each other.

**Examples**:
- A user with `ab.ban.exempt` cannot be banned by anyone.
- A user with `ab.ban.exempt.4` cannot be banned by a user with `ab.ban.exempt.3`, but can be banned by a user with `ab.ban.exempt.5`.
</details>

<details open>
<summary>Additional Notes</summary>

If you are using this plugin on BungeeCord, you need to define permissions in BungeeCord's `config.yml` or manage them via a dedicated BungeeCord permissions plugin.

The BungeeCord permission system does not support the `*` wildcard, so having `ab.*` does not grant access to all commands. To simplify configuration, AdvancedBanZ provides a setting called `EnableAllPermissionNodes`. When enabled, you can use `.all` instead of `.*`. For example, `ab.all` grants permission for all AdvancedBanZ commands. (Note: This feature does not work with negative permissions, e.g., `-ab.all` is invalid.)
</details>

### Configuration File Explanation

#### config.yml

The configuration file should be easy to understand, with detailed comments for each option.

<details open>
<summary>config.yml</summary>

```yaml
# AdvancedBan v4 - Original author Leoko, updated and maintained by 2vY (hlpdev) and Author87668
# Each setting has a brief description; please read carefully before modifying.
# For more information, visit: https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/advancedban.8695/

# Set to false to save all ban records in a local SQLite database
UseMySQL: false

MySQL:
  IP: localhost
  DB-Name: database-name
  Username: admin
  Password: superSecret
  Port: 3306
  Properties: 'verifyServerCertificate=false&useSSL=false&useUnicode=true&characterEncoding=utf8'

# Whether to show only brief logs on plugin enable/disable
DetailedEnableMessage: true
DetailedDisableMessage: true

# Whether to prevent players from joining the server when a database connection error occurs (e.g., MySQL downtime)
LockdownOnError: true

# Default punishment reason (used when none is specified)
# Supports standard color codes or MiniMessage format (https://docs.advntr.dev/minimessage/format.html)
DefaultReason: "No reason provided."

# If the server time differs from your time zone, adjust the offset here
# Example: Server time 16:43, your time 13:43, then set to -3
# You can view server time via /systemPrefs
TimeDiff: 0

# List of commands that muted players cannot use (to prevent bypassing)
MuteCommands:
- 'me'
- 'say'
- 'action'
- 'eaction'
- 'describe'
- 'edescribe'
- 'eme'
- 'w'
- 'm'
- 'pm'
- 'whisper'
- 'ewhisper'
- 'emsg'
- 'msg'
- 'etell'
- 'tell'
- 'er'
- 'r'
- 'reply'
- 'ereply'
- 'ac'
- 'eac'
- 'amsg'
- 'eamsg'
- 'ehelpop'
- 'p msg'

# These players cannot be punished in any way (effective even when offline)
# Recommended to use with the Vault plugin to ensure offline exemptions work correctly
ExemptPlayers:
- 'Leoko'
- 'md5'
- 'dutchy1001'
- 'ItzSomebody'

# Date format for the %DATE% variable
DateFormat: "MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm"

# Whether to enable the .all permission node (for permission systems that do not support *, such as BungeeCord)
# When enabled, ab.all can be used instead of ab.*
# Note: Negative permissions (e.g., -ab.all) are invalid
EnableAllPermissionNodes: false

# UUID Fetcher Settings
UUID-Fetcher:
  # Dynamic mode automatically selects the best fetching method; recommended to keep enabled
  Dynamic: true
  Enabled: true
  Intern: false
  REST-API:
    URL: "https://api.mojang.com/users/profiles/minecraft/%NAME%?at=%TIMESTAMP%"
    Key: "id"
  BackUp-API:
    URL: "https://api.minetools.eu/uuid/%NAME%"
    Key: "id"

# Actions triggered when warnings reach specified counts
# Supports variables: %PLAYER% %REASON% %COUNT%
# Supports MiniMessage format
WarnActions:
  3: "kick %PLAYER% &c&oYou have received your 3rd warning!"
  4: "tempban %PLAYER% 30m &c&oYou have received your 4th warning!"
  5: "tempban %PLAYER% 5h &c&oYou have received your 5th warning!"
  6: "tempban %PLAYER% 7d &c&oYou have received your 6th warning!"
  7: "tempban %PLAYER% 1mo &c&oYou have received your %COUNT%th warning!"
  10: "ban %PLAYER% &c&oYou have received your 10th warning!"

# Maximum punishment duration permission mapping (unit: seconds)
TempPerms:
  1: 600    # 10 minutes
  2: 3600   # 1 hour
  3: 43200  # 12 hours

# Whether to enable debug mode (outputs more logs, useful for troubleshooting)
Debug: false

# Number of days to retain plugin logs (located in plugins/AdvancedBan/logs)
Log Purge Days: 10

# Whether to disable the plugin prefix in all messages
Disable Prefix: false

# Whether to register commands in a friendlier way (Bukkit only)
# Disabled by default to allow overriding /ban and other commands from other plugins
Friendly Register Commands: false
```
</details>

#### messages.yml

Contains all user-facing prompt text, supporting standard color codes and **MiniMessage** format.

<details open>
<summary>messages.yml (excerpt of key structure, full content omitted)</summary>

File structure includes:
- General
- Ban / Ipban / Tempban / Tempipban
- Mute / Tempmute
- Warn / Tempwarn / Note
- Kick
- UnBan / UnMute / UnWarn / UnNote / UnPunish
- Banlist / History / Warns / Notes
- Check

All messages are customizable and support variables such as `%NAME%`, `%OPERATOR%`, `%REASON%`, `%DURATION%`, etc.
</details>

#### layouts.yml

Used to define preset **message templates** and **time increment templates**.

<details open>
<summary>layouts.yml</summary>

```yaml
# Message Templates: Can be called via @TemplateName
Message:
  ExampleLayout:
   - '%PREFIX% &7Banned for cheating'
    - '&c&oExecuted by %OPERATOR%'
    - '&7'
    - "&cDetected use of"
    - "&cillegal client, please stop immediately!"
    - "&cUnban time &8» &7%DURATION%"
    - '&7'
    - '&8Please apply for unban via TS or Forum'
    - "&eTS Address &8» &c&nComing Soon"
    - "&eForum Address &8» &c&nComing Soon"

# Time Templates: Can be called via #TemplateName, duration increases automatically with each punishment
Time:
  ExampleLayout:
   - '30m'   # 1st time
    - '2h'   # 2nd time
    - '1d'   # 3rd time
    - '1w'
    - '1mo'
    - '2mo'
    - '4mo'
    - 'perma' # Permanent
```

**Usage Examples**:
- `/tempban PlayerA #ExampleLayout Cheating`
- `/warn PlayerB @ExampleLayout`
</details>

### Features

- All-in-one system for bans, kicks, mutes, and warnings
- High-performance performance
- Supports both BungeeCord and Bukkit/Spigot/Paper
- Player punishment history
- Advanced UUID support (built-in/external fetchers + backup API)
- Supports MySQL or local SQLite storage
- Fully customizable messages and behaviors
- Multi-line ban/kick messages
- Preset reason templates
- Automatic punishment duration escalation (1st time 1 hour, 2nd time 6 hours...)
- Custom time zone offset
- Automatic warning linkage actions (e.g., auto-kick after 3 warnings)
- `/check` command to query UUID, IP, country, ban/mute/warning status
- Full support for **MiniMessage** formatting syntax

### Technical Support

If you encounter issues, please check the console error logs first. If the problem persists, please submit an issue on our [GitHub Issues page](https://github.com/At87668/AdvancedBanZ/issues/new).

### Statistics

This plugin uses **bStats** to anonymously collect server information (such as player count, server version, etc.).  

**Bukkit**
![Statistics Chart](https://bstats.org/signatures/bukkit/AdvancedBanZ.svg)

**BungeeCord**
![Statistics Chart](https://bstats.org/signatures/bungeecord/AdvancedBanZ.svg)

### API Development

When developing plugin extensions, ensure that the AdvancedBanZ main plugin is installed on the server.

<details open>
<summary>Maven Dependency</summary>

```xml
<repositories>
    ...
    <repository>
        <id>hnt8</id>
        <url>https://java.hnt8.net</url>
    </repository>
    ...
</repositories>

<dependencies>
    ...
    <dependency>
        <groupId>net.hnt8.advancedban</groupId>
        <artifactId>AdvancedBanZ</artifactId>
        <version>3.0.6</version>
        <scope>provided</scope>
    </dependency>
    ...
</dependencies>
```
</details>

title: Refill Chests
description: Allows for chests to be refilled after looting
body:
This mod is meant to be a vanilla friendly version of myLoot, or Lootr. Though it is not exactly the same due to limitations needed to make it remain server side.

Using this mod, it will record every chest that is looted by a player. Then with the run of a command all the chests will be refiled with a new set of loot from their original loot tables.

 

to list out the number of chests that can be refilled use the command /chests list

and to refill them use the command /chests regenerate

 

Please note that you MUST regenerate the loot prior to shutting down a server or instance or the list of looted chests will be lost.

# Loot Multiplier Plus

Adjust loot without rewriting loot tables.

Loot Multiplier Plus gives you simple global multipliers for the biggest loot sources in the game, making it easy to speed up progression, create grindier survival, or tune your server economy.

## What it controls
- Mob drops
- Block drops
- Fishing loot
- Chest loot

## Why use it
- Increase reward rates on casual servers
- Slow progression for harder survival
- Balance custom economies
- Tune overall resource flow with one config file

## Config file
`config/loot-multiplier-plus.json`

Example:

{
  "mob_drops_multiplier": 1.5,
  "block_drops_multiplier": 2.0,

body:
[Support]: https://encode42.dev/support
[Support Badge]: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@intergrav/devins-badges@3/assets/cozy/social/discord-singular_vector.svg

# Natureal
### ˈneɪʧərːiul - A content mod pack based on the concept of nature.

[![Support Badge]][Support]

### ⚙️ Features
**Vanilla-styled**
- Focus on what Minecraft does great: nature!
- All-round consistency.
- World generation mods that enhance Minecraft's fantasy aspect

**Auditory improvements**
- Realistic player and entity footsteps
- Additional sounds when interacting with your environment
- Talk with your friends in immersive environments
- Reverb, occlusion, and drip sounds!

**QOL improvements**
- Chat overhaul with spellcheck, emojis, and better suggestions
- Focus on removing repetitive grind
- ...while moving the game's goalposts further!

**Multiplayer**
- Built by players, for (multi)players
- Ability to upload user-generated audio and photos

**Performance improvements**
- Utilizes the CaffeineMC suite of optimization mods
- Utilizes Iris for fast shaders
- Includes safe and lesser-known performance tweaks
- Strives to include performant content mods
- Not lightweight, but not heavyweight either!

**...and more!**

I did not make any of the projects that make this mod pack possible.  
Make sure to give some love to the authors of the projects listed in [/mods](https://github.com/Encode42/Natureal/tree/main/mods), [/resourcepacks](https://github.com/Encode42/Natureal/tree/main/config/paxi/resourcepacks), and [/shaderpacks](https://github.com/Encode42/Natureal/tree/main/shaderpacks)!

### ❔ FAQ
<details>
<summary>
What makes this different from other mod packs?
</summary>

Natureal's goal is to provide the modded experience, without going too far. This means *everything* is immersive and comprehensible in-game. Through consistency and intuition, this mod pack should be enjoyable for all parties!

For example, there's no minimap mod. *Or so you may think!* You must **craft** the minimap instead! The same goes for the topic of zoom mods; use a spyglass for that!

This was inspired by [Crucial 2](https://github.com/VazkiiMods/crucial2)'s ideology — to keep things vanilla. It's essentially the opposite of mod packs like [All The Mods](https://github.com/AllTheMods), which condense a ton of vastly different mods into their pack.
</details>

<details>
<summary>
The game is consistently stuttering! Why?
</summary>

This is likely due to [Java's GC](https://how-java-works.yht.one/) being run.

This is normal, and can be mitigated by allocating more memory to your client. I recommend `6 GB` as a minimum! You can also use [flags.sh](https://flags.sh) to generate a launcher profile using [Aikar's flags](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/aikars-flags) and your specified amount of memory.
</details>

<details>
<summary>
Does this work with OptiFine?
</summary>

No. Nor is this fully* compatible with OptiFine resource packs. Natureal mod pack uses Sodium, Iris, etc.

\* Natureal includes a few mods that add resource pack features from OptiFine, but Natureal itself doesn't aim to be fully OptiFine-compatible.
</details>

<details>
<summary>
If this is a nature mod pack, why are there technology mods?
</summary>

Unfortunately, many of the nature-based replacements for tech mods aren't up to my standards. For example, chest-based storage systems don't have what makes AE2 great in my opinion; crafting patterns. As such, I decided to include a couple of technology mods to fill that gap. The pack's primary focus is still nature, though.

It's your choice whether to use these mods! Alternatives such as Create are provided and supported for those that prefer a more kinetic world.

As for the Dr. Who related mods, they were added by request of the Natureal's testers. Why not?
</details>

<details>
<summary>
I can't sleep!
</summary>

Press space. 😄
</details>

<details>
<summary>
What in the world does the summary mean?
</summary>

It's a quote from Thom Yorke's *[Analyze](https://youtu.be/MnMUdko6ljs?t=105)*, a song on an album regarding human issues. I felt it was fitting for a mod pack focused on nature!

If you're running a dedicated server using this pack, you may notice multiple quotes mentioning nature in the MOTD. I'm not sure who said these. I just took them from a list I found online.
</details>

**✅ Also included in this modpack:**

- ✨️ **Butter smooth GUI**
- 🏔️ **Distant Horizon and BSL shaders** for beautiful effects and world views

# **Compatibility**

✅ MedieCraft

✅ MedieCraft - Lite

✅ MedieCraft - Server

❌ MedieCraft - Cross-Platform

❌ MedieCraft - Lite - Cross-Platform

❌ MedieCraft - Server - Cross-Platform

❌ MC Bedrock Clients

❌ MC Java Clients (using Fabric, ViaVersion, ViaFabric, CreativeCore and GeckoLib)

# **Key notes**
- **Client side modpack** (necessary to play in solo worlds and in server worlds using [MedieCraft - Server])
- **Highly Detailed ModPack** (check [MedieCraft - Lite](https://modrinth.com/modpack/mediecraft-lite) if you don't have a dedicated graphics card)
- The mod list is available by clicking on 'versions' and then on the version number you chose to install.
- If your **game is lagging**, you can disable all added particles in 'Video Settings' menu, as well as shaders if you want to decrease/increase quality. Keep in mind that Distant Horizon is quite hard to run smoothly on mid-end PCs, you can disable or tweak it in the settings, beside the FOV setting.

# **System Requirements**
**Minimal System Requirements (without shaders & without Distant Horizon mod)**

- 2GB allocated to Minecraft

- 4 Cores / 4-8 Threads CPU (AMD Ryzen 3 3100, Intel Core i5 7400)

- NVIDIA GeForce GT 1050Ti 4GB, RX 560 4GB

- 8Gb RAM 

- 1,5GB SSD storage


**Recommended System Requirements (w/ shaders & without Distant Horizon mod)**

- 4GB allocated to Minecraft

- 6 Cores / 12 Threads CPU (AMD Ryzen 5 5600, Intel Core i5 12400F)

- NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 6GB, AMD Radeon RX580 8GB

- 16GB RAM

- 1,5GB SSD storage


**Optimal System Requirements (w/ shaders ultra preset & Distant Horizon mod)**

- 6-8GB allocated to Minecraft (depending on Distant Horizon configuration)

- 8 Cores / 16 Threads CPU (AMD Ryzen 7 5700X, Intel Core i7 12700)

- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060, AMD Radeon Vega 56

- 32GB RAM

- 1,5GB SSD storage

# **Instructions**

1. Download this modpack with the version you chose or the same version running your server.
2. Go to your Modrinth library and click on 'Play'. Game should start and you are ready to go!


# **Q&A**

- **Why is there a [MedieCraft](https://modrinth.com/modpack/mediecraft) and [MedieCraft - Lite](https://modrinth.com/modpack/mediecraft-lite) modpack ? What's the difference between the two ?**

[MedieCraft](https://modrinth.com/modpack/mediecraft) (this one) has many client side mods that improve quality of life like [Smooth GUI](https://modrinth.com/mod/smooth-gui), [Camera Overhaul](https://modrinth.com/mod/cameraoverhaul), [Particular](https://modrinth.com/mod/particular), [BSL](https://modrinth.com/shader/bsl-shaders), [Distant Horizons](https://modrinth.com/mod/distanthorizons), [First-person Model](https://modrinth.com/mod/first-person-model) and many other mods compared to [MedieCraft - Lite](https://modrinth.com/modpack/mediecraft-lite) which doesn't.

- **Is this modpack compatible with [MedieCraft - Server](https://modrinth.com/modpack/mediecraft-server) ?** 

Absolutely, using this modpack you can join your solo worlds as well as servers using the [MedieCraft - Server](https://modrinth.com/modpack/mediecraft-server) modpack on server side.

- **How much RAM should I allocate to this modpack profile ?**

6GB minimum if you are using [BSL shaders](https://modrinth.com/shader/bsl-shaders) and [Distant Horizons](https://modrinth.com/mod/distanthorizons). 4GB should be fine by disabling them.

- **Can I play this modpack in older versions of Minecraft ?**

Yes, to be able to play in older versions, you have to unlink the modpack at the very bottom of the modpack options. Then change the version of Minecraft and update all mods by clicking on 'update mods'. Start the game and it should launch if all mods are compatible with the selected version of Minecraft.

- **Is this modpack Cross-Platform ?**

No, but I recreated this modpack with only Cross-Platform mods. See [MedieCraft - Cross-Platform](https://modrinth.com/modpack/mediecraft-cross-platform).

- **Can I use this modpack with a server running [MedieCraft - Server - Cross-Platform](https://modrinth.com/modpack/mediecraft-server-cross-platform) ?** 

No, a network protocol error will be raised. See [MedieCraft - Cross-Platform](https://modrinth.com/modpack/mediecraft-cross-platform).



# **Credits**
💙 Huge thanks to Maffhew with his Excalibur resource pack for giving me the idea of creating this resource pack. I honored him by putting his resource pack icon to my modpack ! The resource pack is in this modpack !
