title: Hollow Steve [HORROR]
description: Adds Hollow Steve, a horror stalker boss that haunts you, grows stronger after each defeat, and must be killed 10 times to survive.
body:
![HollowSteve](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/b89be3cfe6f1a5de7adf79b236cd18919ac5af6a_0.webp)
# Hollow Steve - A horror stalker boss that learns every time you kill it

**Hollow Steve** is a horror survival boss mod for Minecraft. It adds a tall, broken Steve-like entity that does not simply spawn and attack like a normal mob. It watches first.

From **Day 1**, your world starts to feel wrong. You may hear footsteps behind you, see smoke appear nearby, or notice something standing still in the distance. Hollow Steve can appear, stare, vanish, and disturb the player before the real fight even begins.

For the first two days, he is not fully hunting yet.

On **Day 3**, the haunting becomes a hunt.

Every time you kill Hollow Steve, he returns the next Minecraft day stronger than before. He gains more health, more damage, more speed, more reach, and more dangerous behavior. To end the Hollow permanently, you must defeat him **10 times**.

## ✨ Features

- **Horror progression from Day 1**
  - The mod starts slowly with stalking, sounds, apparitions, and strange events.
  - Hollow Steve does not immediately behave like a normal boss.

- **Day 1 and Day 2 haunting phase**
  - Hollow Steve can appear near the player.
  - He may stare, vanish, or create unsettling moments.
  - Fake footsteps, breathing, whispers, smoke, and darkness effects can happen.
  - One early apparition can hit the player once before disappearing.

- **Day 3+ hunt phase**
  - Hollow Steve begins attacking for real.
  - He chases the player, uses long-arm melee attacks, and becomes an active threat.
  - Later phases become much more aggressive.

- **10-phase boss progression**
  - Kill 1 makes him return stronger.
  - Kill 2 makes him more dangerous.
  - Every defeat pushes him closer to his final form.
  - Phase 10 is the final version of Hollow Steve.

- **Escalating combat**
  - More health each phase
  - More damage each phase
  - Faster movement
  - Longer attack reach
  - Strong knockback
  - Faster attack pressure
  - More threatening teleport and vanish behavior

- **Creepy anomaly system**
  - Fake footsteps behind the player
  - Breathing sounds
  - Whisper-like sounds
  - Low growls
  - Glitch-like sounds
  - Smoke and soul particles
  - Darkness and slowness effects

- **GeckoLib animated entity**
  - Idle animation
  - Walk animation
  - Chase animation
  - Stare animation
  - Attack animation
  - Hurt animation
  - Spawn animation
  - Vanish animation
  - Death animation
  - Final death animation

- **Cinematic spawn moments**
  - Smoke bursts
  - Soul particles
  - Portal particles
  - Growls
  - Heartbeat sounds
  - Darkness pressure

- **Anti-cheese behavior**
  - Hollow Steve can punish simple abuse strategies.
  - Boats and similar escape tricks are not always safe.
  - Hiding behind blocks becomes less reliable in later phases.
  - Mobs that attack Hollow Steve can be punished heavily.

- **Survival rewards**
  - Defeating Hollow Steve gives rewards to help the player survive future phases.
  - Rewards include totems, potions, enchanted armor, weapons, arrows, and enchanted golden apples.

- **Clear final victory**
  - Defeat Hollow Steve 10 times.
  - Trigger the final death.
  - End the haunting permanently.

## 🩸 What happens in-game?

### Day 1
The world begins normally, but something is wrong.

Hollow Steve may appear as an apparition. He may stand nearby, stare at you, or vanish when seen. One early encounter can hit the player once before disappearing. The goal of Day 1 is not full combat. It is tension.

You are meant to feel watched.

### Day 2
The haunting continues.

The strange sounds and apparition encounters become more noticeable. Hollow Steve still does not fully fight like a boss yet, but the player should understand that something is coming.

Day 2 is the warning.

### Day 3
The hunt begins.

Hollow Steve can now spawn as a real hostile boss. He can chase, attack, teleport, vanish, and pressure the player. From here onward, killing him is required to progress.

### After each kill
When Hollow Steve dies, he does not return again on the same Minecraft day.

The next day, he comes back stronger.

### Kill 10
The final death happens.

Hollow Steve fades permanently, the haunting ends, and the player wins.

## 🎁 Reward progression

Hollow Steve becomes stronger after each death, so the player is rewarded with survival tools after defeating him.

Rewards can include:

- Totems of Undying
- Healing potions
- Speed potions
- Night Vision potions
- Milk buckets to help against blindness
- Enchanted netherite armor
- Powerful enchanted netherite sword
- Enchanted bow
- Arrow stacks
- Enchanted golden apples

These rewards are meant to help the player survive the later phases, especially when Hollow Steve becomes much faster and more aggressive.

## 🔧 Requirements

- **Minecraft**: 26.1.2
- **Available loaders**:
  - Fabric Loader and Fabric API
  - NeoForge
- **Required library**:
  - GeckoLib
- **Planned loaders**:
  - Quilt *(planned)*
  - Forge *(planned)*
- **Java**: 25+
- **Environment**: Client and server required

## 📖 How to play

1. Install Hollow Steve, Fabric API, and GeckoLib.
2. Start or load a world.
3. Survive Day 1 and Day 2.
4. Prepare before Day 3.
5. Fight Hollow Steve when the hunt begins.
6. Kill him whenever he returns.
7. Survive all 10 phases.
8. Defeat the final Hollow Steve and end the haunting.

## ⚠️ Horror notice

Hollow Steve is designed as a horror progression mod. It includes sudden sounds, darkness effects, stalking behavior, jumpscare-like moments, and escalating combat pressure.

title: Title Damage Indicator
description: This is a simple mod for the Fabric Loader, that displays health changes (damage/healing) of targeted entities in a quick, vanilla title.
body:
**⚠️IMPORTANT⚠️**

This mod requires [Fabric API](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api).

<hr>

**Mod Description**

**Title Damage Indicator** is a client-sided only mod for the **Fabric Loader**, that allows you to see health changes of entities that you are targeting (looking at), in a Minecraft vanilla **subtitle**. For example, if the entity that you are looking at took damage, then a subtitle would appear, containing this text: "_-1 [19 LEFT]_". And as for healing, this: "_+1 [NOW AT 20]_". If the entity that you are targeting dies, then the subtitle will display as (example): "_-3 [DEAD]_", and a high-pitched player exp level up sound will play ("minecraft:entity.player.levelup", with a pitch of 1.25). And if it heals to its max health, then it will display as (also example): "_+2 [FULLY HEALED]_"; and a sound will play ("minecraft:entity.witch.drink", with a pitch of 1.0). The whole mod is toggleable with the **/toggletitledamageindicator** command. 

For a visual of this mod, please play the **Mod Demonstration Video Below**, or check out this mod's screenshots in the **[Gallery Tab](https://modrinth.com/mod/title-damage-indicator/gallery)**.

title: CozyRosie's Bunis!
description: A goofy nuisance creature here to brighten up (and terrorize) your day!
body:
CozyRosie's Bunis bring a twinge of silliness and whimsy to your Minecraft world.

Bunis (pronounced like "Bunnies") are not quite the fuzzy forest friends you're familiar with. These guys are dubious little cosmic critters, chewing their way through stars and dimensions to find all kinds of fun things to eat and mischief to get up to. 

More of meta-cartoon than living creature, they're as adorable and charming as they are a nuisance to gameplay. One does not "fight" or "farm" the bunis, but work around and trick them into doing things that help you.

A buni's favorite things include:
- Eating picked ferns and flowers
- Eating ANY stray items left on the ground (it's okay, they don't digest it, they just store it, up to a single full stack)
- Hitting each other with hammers
- Mitosis (use an axe)
- Busting it down when they hear music
- Automation - eating a dye ingredient produces twice as much
- Being dressed up with dye colors
- Being picked up and tossed arounnd
- Not taking damage - which is great, because they never do :)

They dislike:
- Being swatted at too much
- Seeing their friends get hurt
- Placed soul torches/lanterns/fires [SCARY!!! :<]

Bunis spawn close to the world spawn, under any block open to the sky, and appear less often as you go further out. Keep an eye out for rare variants in other dimensions!

Also features a config for how aggressively likely bunis are likely to bop each other/hostile entities/players, their spawn rates, spawn cap, and a serverside whitelist tag to add entities that they attack, plus a gamerule to manually turn on/off their natural spawning.

A quick summary:

title: Experience Nuggets
description: Adds Experience Nuggets for item-based XP storage and transfer!
body:
⚠️ IMPORTANT: USAGE GUIDELINES
If you're planning to use this on a server or modpack,
please refer to:
https://gamedash43.github.io/dash-mcl-licenses/#usage

![Title Text "Experience Nuggets"](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/7c9d1ca63be5252c2a42d45e8ed5c992ea5a08db.png)
Experience Nuggets adds the ability to store and transport experience points as items.

# 📜 How to Use

### 1. Creating Experience Nuggets
- **Via Hopper Conversion:**  
  - Lead experience orbs into a vanilla hopper.  
  - The hopper converts the orbs into experience nuggets based on their value.
- **Manual Collection:**  
  - Stand on a hopper, shift, and look down.  
  - Hold until the hopper absorbs the desired amount of experience, converting it into an item.
- **Item Movement:**  
  - Once created, experience nuggets can be moved around like any other item.

### 2. Using Experience Nuggets
- **Placing Nuggets:**  
  - Right-click an experience nugget to place it, which releases an experience orb containing its stored value.
- **Using in Dispensers:**  
  - Experience nuggets can also be loaded into dispensers to dispense the stored experience when activated.

# ❓ FAQ

<details>
<summary>Why is there no experience merging feature?</summary>
I developed a script for merging experience, but it resulted in over nine different experience orb values per automatic farm, complicating filtering and storage.
</details>

<details>
<summary>How optimized is this add-on?</summary>
This datapack is a proof of concept and not fully optimized. It will continue to receive updates, but unless it gains popularity, a completely optimized version may not be released.
</details>
<details>
<summary>How do I report a bug?</summary>
Join the Discord and either DM me or post a message in the reports channel.
</details>

<details>
<summary>How do I uninstall this add-on?</summary>
Just run the command "/function dash.exp:uninstall"
</details>

title: Enhanced Villagers
description: More realistic villagers
body:
# Villager Mod

Minecraft mod that enhances the villagers.

Core idea is to enhance villagers to make them act more like players, based on the existing vanilla logic.

## Current features

- Real villager trade
  - Will only trade what is in their inventory (no more magic item spawning)
  - Trades will update villagers inventory
- Villager has larger inventor (36 slot like the player)
- Villager want to buy food when needed
- Villager will sell excess food
- Every villagers will trade (including uemployed, nitwit and children)

## Future features

- Merchant profession
- Real villagers crafting
  - Will only craft what is craftable from what is in their inventory
  - Will need tools / machines
- Villager will buy what they need for crafting
- Villager picks up any dropped items (like they pick up some food items)
- Villager to villager trade
- Configurable trades

title: Glidelytra: An Elytra Rebalance Mod
description: Rebalancing the Elytra in a fun way. Inspiration taken from the legacy console glide minigame
body:
# Intro

Glidelyta Aims to fix the issues with the all powerful mode of transportation, the elytra.

Glidelytra (Glide-lytra) is a Minecraft Mod for Fabric that Aims to rebalance the Elytra in a fun way.

This mod is a work in progress Beta and some major things might change.

## The Content
Inspired by the Legacy console edition Glide minigame, this mod features boost rings!

Boost rings are multiblocks that boost you when you fly above them!
When you get boosted you will gain a status effect that makes you have less drag while gliding.
Check out the Wiki for more Info on how to build the multiblock.

![A boost ring](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/d9675f279ae4fd16cd61686eff5177d9a8ae0212.png)

Firework Rockets now have a cooldown and their cooldown increases slightly per flight durration.

Your Elytra will also recharge durrability slowly when you're not flying.

When you get hit by a projectile or take damage from an explosion, your elytra will be disabled
for a little while, preventing them from escaping quickly in pvp matches or sniping gliders out of the sky.

Fireworks have an additional boost while under Y level 90.
Effect is greater the closer you are to sea level.

Elytra has less gravity and less drag overall.

## Game Psychology

To achive maximum efficency, you will have to build a network of boost rings to keep your speed. They are more powerful at high altitudes with sea level (y63) being the base level.
your elytra will be constantly loosing durrability as you fly so its important that you get
where you're going quickly. Firework rockets are still viable for short distances and
getting a little altitude but the elytra won't be something that you can use to rapidly explore undeveloped chunks with as you will need to take breaks for it to recharge.

### Extra Content
Featuring 7 music discs with soundtracks from the minecraft glide minigame (By Gareth Coker)!

These Soundtracks are on the "Minecraft Creator-safe" playlist so I assume its ok to use them.
If im wrong, tell me and I'll remove them. 
Treat these as beta content that could go away in the future.

This Mod Features a very basic config. Check the Wiki for info on the config options.

title: CobbleStacker
description: CobbleStacker is a server-side Fabric mod that reduces lag by automatically merging nearby identical mobs, ground items, and spawners into a single entity with a stack counter, fully compatible with Cobblemon.
body:
CobbleStacker is a server-side Fabric mod for Minecraft 1.21 designed to significantly reduce entity lag by intelligently stacking mobs, ground items, and spawners. Fully compatible with Cobblemon — all Pokemon are         
  automatically excluded from stacking.                                                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Mob Stacking                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  - Automatically merges nearby identical mobs into a single entity with a visible nametag (e.g. "x16 Zombie")                                                                                                                   
  - Respects mob attributes: variant, color, size, baby/adult, tamed owner, profession, and more                                                                                                                               
  - Configurable death behavior: KILL_ONE (kills one and respawns the stack with reduced count) or KILL_ALL (kills the entire stack with multiplied drops and XP)                                                                
  - Entities with name tags can be excluded from stacking                                                                                                                                                                      
  - Blacklist support by entity type and world

  Item Stacking

  - Merges ground items of the same type beyond vanilla limits (up to 1024 per stack by default)
  - Custom nametags showing the real item count
  - Built-in auto-clear system that removes old item stacks after a configurable time, with a whitelist for valuable items
  - Manual clearlag command for instant cleanup

  Spawner Stacking

  - Stack multiple spawners of the same type by right-clicking with a spawner in hand
  - Floating hologram displays the spawner type and stack count
  - Mobs spawned from stacked spawners come out pre-stacked
  - Silk Touch support for spawner drops
  - Automatic spawner property repair to prevent broken spawners
  - Persistent data saved to JSON

  General

  - Fully configurable via cobblestacker.json
  - Admin commands: /cobblestacker reload, stats, info, kill, clear, clearlag, debug, fixspawner, setstack
  - Lightweight and optimized with batch processing, caching, and minimal overhead
  - No client-side installation required

title: Text Placeholder API Expressions
description: Adds math, conditional, and string manipulation expressions to Text Placeholder API.
body:
# Text Placeholder API Expressions
Adds math, conditional, and string manipulation expressions to Text Placeholder API.  
This project uses [Keval](https://github.com/notKamui/Keval) for parsing math expressions, and would have been exponentially more difficult without it. Show the author some love and star his repo!

### Using Placeholders In Expressions
This extension uses the `${category:placeholder}` syntax to allow supplying placeholders that resolve to numbers as components.  
For example; to display a player's health as a percentage (such as within the tab list), you could use the following:  
`%expr:math ${player:health} * 100 / ${player:max_health}%%`

## Math Placeholder
The bulk of the additions (no pun intended) in this extension are accessed through the `expr:math` placeholder.

You can think of this placeholder as handling three distinct 'types':  
 * Components, such as numbers, functions, constants, and placeholders that resolve to numbers.
 * Binary operators, such as addition or subtraction, which go between two components.
 * Unary operators, such as negation and factorial, which apply to a single component.

### Components and operators supplied by this extension
Binary operators are applied between two components.
| Binary Operator | Function | Example              | Result
| :-------------- | :------- | :------------------- | :-----
| +               | Add      | `%expr:math 2 + 2%`  | 4
| -               | Subtract | `%expr:math 4 - 1%`  | 3
| *               | Multiply | `%expr:math 3 * 3%`  | 9
| /               | Divide   | `%expr:math 9 / 4%`  | 2.25
| ^               | Exponent | `%expr:math 3 ^ 3%`  | 27

Unary operators are applied to a single component.
| Unary Operator | Function  | Example              | Result
| :------------- | :-------- | :------------------- | :-----
| -              | Negate    | `%expr:math 1 + -1%` | 0
| +              | Identity  | `%expr:math ??%`     | What does this even do
| !              | Factorial | `%expr:math 5!%`     | 120

Functions are components, taking expressions as arguments.
| Function | Arguments | Description                    | Example                      | Result
| :------- | :-------- | :----------------------------- | :--------------------------- | :----
| mod      | 2         | Modulo / remainder             | `%expr:math mod(7, 2)%`      | 1
| neg      | 1         | Negate / invert (Like unary -) | `%expr:math neg(10)%`        | -10
| abs      | 1         | Absolute value                 | `%expr:math abs(-10)%`       | 10
| sqrt     | 1         | Square root                    | `%expr:math sqrt(34)%`       | 5.8309
| cbrt     | 1         | Cube root                      | `%expr:math cbrt(30)%`       | 3.1072
| exp      | 1         | Exponential                    | `%expr:math exp(4)%`         | 54.5981
| ln       | 1         | Natural logarithm              | `%expr:math ln(4)%`          | 1.3862
| log10    | 1         | Base 10 logarithm              | `%expr:math log10(4)%`       | 0.6020
| log2     | 1         | Base 2 logarithm               | `%expr:math log2(4)%`        | 2
| rad      | 1         | Degrees to radians             | `%expr:math rad(30)%`        | 0.5235
| sin      | 1         | Sine                           | `%expr:math sin(rad(30))%`   | 0.4999
| cos      | 1         | Cosine                         | `%expr:math cos(rad(30))%`   | 0.8660
| tan      | 1         | Tangent                        | `%expr:math tan(rad(30))%`   | 0.5773
| asin     | 1         | Arcsine                        | `%expr:math asin(rad(30))%`  | 0.5510
| acos     | 1         | Arccosine                      | `%expr:math acos(rad(30))%`  | 1.0197
| atan     | 1         | Arctangent                     | `%expr:math atan(rad(30))%`  | 0.4823
| ceil     | 1         | Round up                       | `%expr:math ceil(0.4)%`      | 1
| floor    | 1         | Round down                     | `%expr:math floor(0.6)%`     | 0
| round    | 1         | Round                          | `%expr:math round(0.5)%`     | 1
| min      | 2+        | Smallest argument              | `%expr:math min(1, 0.3, 7)%` | 0.3
| max      | 2+        | Largest argument               | `%expr:math max(1, 0.3, 7)%` | 7
| avg      | 2+        | Average of arguments           | `%expr:math avg(1, 0.3, 7)%` | 2.7666

Constants are components which resolve to a constant value.
| Constant | Description    |
| :------- | :------------- |
| PI       | π              |
| e        | Euler's number |

## Conditional Placeholders
Arguments to these placeholders must be separated by semicolons (`;`) instead of spaces.

### `%expr:ifeq%`
Test whether `a` and `b` are equal, and return `c` or `d` depending on the result.

`%expr:ifeq aIsMath a bIsMath b cIsMath c dIsMath d%`
| Argument | Description
| :------- | :----------
| aIsMath  | Whether to parse `a` as a math expression. Either `true` or `false`.
| a        | Math expression or text to compare against b. If treated as text, and spaces at the start or end of the string are removed.
| bIsMath  | Whether to parse `b` as a math expression. Either `true` or `false`.
| b        | Math expression or text to compare against a. If treated as text, and spaces at the start or end of the string are removed.
| cIsMath  | Whether to parse `c` as a math expression. Either `true` or `false`.
| c        | Math expression or text to use if `a` and `b` are equal.
| dIsMath  | Whether to parse `d` as a math expression. Either `true` or `false`.
| d        | Math expression or text to use if `a` and `b` are not equal.

#### Example
`Player %expr:ifeq false; ${player:equipment_slot mainhand}; false; Diamond Sword; false; is; false; is not% holding a Diamond Sword.`
| Condition                                             | Result
| :---------------------------------------------------- | :-----
| `%player:equipment_slot mainhand% == "Diamond Sword"` | Player is holding a Diamond Sword.
| `%player:equipment_slot mainhand% != "Diamond Sword"` | Player is not holding a Diamond Sword.

### `%expr:iflt%`
Test whether `a` is less than `b`, and return `c` or `d` depending on the result.

`%expr:iflt a b cIsMath c dIsMath d%`
| Argument | Description
| :------- | :----------
| a        | Math expression to compare against b.
| b        | Math expression to compare against a.
| cIsMath  | Whether to parse `c` as a math expression. Either `true` or `false`.
| c        | Math expression or text to use if `a` is less than `b`.
| dIsMath  | Whether to parse `d` as a math expression. Either `true` or `false`.
| d        | Math expression or text to use if `a` is not less than `b`.

#### Example
`Player is in %expr:iflt ${player:health}; 14; false; poor; false; good% health`
| Condition               | Result
| :---------------------- | :-----
| `%player:health% < 14`  | Player is in poor health
| `%player:health% >= 14` | Player is in good health

### `%expr:ifgt%`
Test whether `a` is greater than `b`, and return `c` or `d` depending on the result.

`%expr:ifgt a b cIsMath c dIsMath d%`
| Argument | Description
| :------- | :----------
| a        | Math expression to compare against b.
| b        | Math expression to compare against a.
| cIsMath  | Whether to parse `c` as a math expression. Either `true` or `false`.
| c        | Math expression or text to use if `a` is greater than `b`.
| dIsMath  | Whether to parse `d` as a math expression. Either `true` or `false`.
| d        | Math expression or text to use if `a` is not greater than `b`.

#### Example
`Health: %expr:ifgt ${player:health}; 4; true; ${player:health} * 100 / ${player:max_health}%; false; Nearly dead!%`
| Condition               | Result
| :---------------------- | :-----
| `%player:health% == 15` | Health: 75
| `%player:health% == 14` | Health: 70
| `%player:health% <= 4`  | Health: Nearly dead!

## String Placeholders
Arguments to these placeholders must be separated by semicolons (`;`) instead of spaces.

### `%expr:pad%`, `%expr:padleft%`, and `%expr:padright%`
Pad one or both sides of `str` with `c` until the string length reaches `length`.

`%expr:pad length; str; c%`
`%expr:padleft length; str; c%`
`%expr:padright length; str; c%`
| Argument | Description
| :------- | :----------
| length   | Math expression, target length of the padded string.
| str      | Source string to pad. Spaces at the start or end of the string are removed.
| c        | Character to use for padding.

#### Example
`%expr:padleft 2 ${server:online} 0% / %server:max_players%`
| Condition               | Result
| :---------------------- | :-----
| `%server:online% == 12` | 12 / 40
| `%server:online% == 4`  | 04 / 40

### `%expr:padmatch%`, `%expr:padmatchleft%`, and `%expr:padmatchright%`
Pad one or both sides of `str` with `c` until the string length matches the length of `match`.

`%expr:padmatch match; str; c%`
`%expr:padmatchleft match; str; c%`
`%expr:padmatchright match; str; c%`
| Argument | Description
| :------- | :----------
| match    | String to match the length of. Spaces at the start or end of the string are removed.
| str      | Source string to pad. Spaces at the start or end of the string are removed.
| c        | Character to use for padding.

#### Example
`%expr:padmatchleft ${server:max_players} ${server:online} 0% / %server:max_players%`
| Condition                                           | Result
| :-------------------------------------------------- | :-----
| `%server:max_players% == 40, %server:online% == 4`  | 04 / 40
| `%server:max_players% == 100, %server:online% == 4` | 004 / 100

body:

#### **This datapack uses experimental features!**  
#### **Please make a backup before adding this pack to an existing world!** 

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/AfcoarzWisk" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe>

### **Resource Pack Required**
#### To find the relevant resource pack, go to the page for the specific datapack [version](https://modrinth.com/datapack/photocraft-dp/versions) you are trying to install!

# Photocraft Datapack

![Animated comparison of photographed region and resulting photograph](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/46cc0f1f3218e1e99e1087b2901571e6f5bace23.gif)  

This datapack adds a camera that can be used to create map-art "photos" of the world.  
There are two items and recipes added to the game - the camera itself, and photo paper.  

You can craft a Camera with 3 Black Carpet, 2 Iron Ingots, 2 Redstone, 1 Spyglass, and 1 Lightning Rod:  
![Crafting Recipe for Camera](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/3aea455c1586c4574ff255d9d4e4de3dbf879711.png)

You can craft 4 pieces of Photo Paper with 3 Resin, 3 Paper, 1 Cyan Dye, 1 Yellow Dye, and 1 Magenta Dye:  
![Crafting Recipe for Photo Paper](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/67390af0ff14a083de57c97b67939ccf3a359a22.png)

To use the camera, click and hold the use-item button. This will pull up a viewfinder that will provide a frame of what will be included in the photo. Releasing the use-item button will place the camera in the world.  
![Example of Viewfinder](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/66d0b3f55e930c8e495ee793af78f2b3857cac99_0.webp)

To take a photo, click the use-item button on the camera while holding a piece of photo paper. The camera will start emitting smoke particles and the lights on the back of the camera will start turning on, showing photo progress.  
![A Camera generating a photo](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/bb9d8fd093d0f5c3a6c7f1800f631dd64e049930_0.webp)

When the camera is done exposing the photo, the lights on the back will turn green and the camera will play a sound.  
![A camera that is done generating a photo](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/75240d36ae1292da9aeee9c35cd98a1c8a4c6537.png)

Right click the camera with an empty hand to retrieve the final photo.  
![A finalized photo](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/17e3a61364318e395e390b66782c2b03e96d12bb.png)

At any point, other than when retrieving a photo, left-clicking the camera will cause it to break, dropping a camera. Any photo that is stored in the camera **will be lost** if it is not retrieved first!

title: Soul RPG Stats
description:

Still in its early days
sorry for the bad explanation
body:
Soul RPG Stats is a simple customizable RPG style leveling and stats mod for 1.19.2

Created Using MCreator

at the moment it is quite bare bones so bare with the dev process

the first thing to do is to either open the stats gui with the hotkey "P by default" or craft a Stats Orb Like with:
 - 1 Glass Block
 - 1 Amethyst
 - 1 Gold Nugget

The recipe is shapeless so you don't need to worry about the order

xp is currently only added by xp orbs (there will be other methods later)

the xp curve is controlled by gamerules that can be edited by a server admin for full customization
 - EXP Base - The Amount of XP to get from LVL 1 to 2 Default 50
 - EXP Power - The amount the XP requirement increase by each LVL

the XP Curve is calculated with "EXP Base" * ( "Player LVL" ^ "EXP Power" )

two more gamerules are available to server admins:
 - Max Level - The Max Level Someone can have - Default 200
   - -1 and below for infinite Levels
   - 0 and 1 to disable Leveling Up
   - 2 and above to enable
 - SP Per Level - Amount of Skill Points Awarded Per Level - Default 10

Sp or Skill Points can be used to buy Stat Bonuses of the following stats:
 - STR or Strength - Modifies Attack Damage and Knockback
 - DEX or Dexterity - Modifies Attack Speed
 - CON or Constitution - Modifies Health and Natural Armor
 - INT or Intelligence - Currently Useless
 - WIS or Wisdom - Currently Useless
 - CHA or Charisma - Modifies Luck

to be added:
 - More EXP Generation Methods
 - Compatibility With Ars Nouveau
 - More Stat Effects and Modifiers
 - More Admin Commands
 - Compatibility With Curios API

This Mod is free to use in mod packs with attribution

title: SimplePlayerWarps
description: A simple Paper Minecraft plugin that lets players create "warps" themselves and others can teleport to.
body:
![banner](https://github.com/ImCodist/simple-player-warps/assets/50346006/eb747521-73da-4959-bfd9-bd279021b2f2)

**SimplePlayerWarps** is **exactly** what the name says it is.
The plugin offers a solution for a *"player warps"* system, where each player has control over their own set of warps players can teleport to and visit from anywhere.

And that's it! The plugin aims to do *exactly* what it says and to do it the best it can.

I plan to add a plethora of customization options so you can mold to plugin exactly to your liking, for whatever kind of server you're running.

## Commands
- `/warp <name>` - Teleports the player to a created warp.
- `/warps [player]` - Returns a list of warps the player can teleport to.
- `/warpset <name>` - Creates a warp at a position for players to teleport to.
- `/warpdel <name>` - Deletes an existing warp.
- `/warpedit <name> [property] [value]` - Edit a property of an existing warp.
- `/warpinfo <name>` - Returns basic information on a warp. (i.e location, creator, world)
- `/warpreload` - Reloads configuration and warps.

## Permissions
- `simpleplayerwarps.warp` - Allows a user to teleport to a warp. (default: true)
- `simpleplayerwarps.warps` - Allows a user to view every created warp. (default: true)
- `simpleplayerwarps.warpset` - Allows a user to create a warp. (default: true)
- `simpleplayerwarps.warpdel` - Allows a user to delete warps they own. (default: true)
- `simpleplayerwarps.warpedit` - Allows a user to edit warps they own. (default: true)
- `simpleplayerwarps.warpinfo` - Allows a user to view information on a warp. (default: true)
- `simpleplayerwarps.warpreload` - Reloads the plugins configuration and warps folder. (default: op)
- `simpleplayerwarps.warpset.infinite` - Allows a user to create infinite warps. (default: op)
- `simpleplayerwarps.warpdel.others` - Allows a user to delete others warps. (default: op)
- `simpleplayerwarps.warpedit.others` - Allows a user to edit others warps. (default: op)
- `simpleplayerwarps.warpedit.advanced` - Allows a user to edit advanced values of a warp like position and author. (default: op)
- `simpleplayerwarps.warps.private` - Allows a user to view private warps. (default: op)
- `simpleplayerwarps.privatewarps` - Allows a user to create private warps. (default: true)

### NOTE: SimplePlayerWarps is ONLY for Paper servers (and loaders that use it as a base) as of right now. I will consider downgrading to Spigot if the demand is high enough.

title: Let Me Sleep
description: Monsters keeping you awake? Customize sleeping, waking, and bed mechanics freely.
body:
Let Me Sleep gives you full control over Minecraft's sleeping experience. 🌙 From bedtime restrictions to waking up refreshed, nearly every part of sleeping can be customized to better fit your world and playstyle.

Trouble finding the monster keeping you awake? Beds refusing to work when they should? Want sleeping to heal, clear effects, or simply feel smoother? This mod makes nights more flexible, less frustrating, and far more configurable. ✨

  • 🌙 Smarter Sleeping: Sleep during rain, wake up instantly, and enjoy a smooth falling asleep animation.
  • 👁️ Reveal Nearby Monsters: Monsters preventing sleep can briefly glow and play ambient sounds so they are easier to find.
  • 😌 Relaxed Monster Checks: Persistent, unreachable, or peaceful nearby monsters can optionally be ignored when sleeping.
  • 🛏️ Flexible Bed Rules: Remove range, obstruction, or monster checks to make beds less restrictive.
  • ❤️ Restorative Sleep: Configure sleeping to restore health or adjust hunger when waking up.
  • ☀️ Weather Control: Optionally reset the weather cycle when waking up for calmer mornings ahead.
  • 🧪 Wake Up Effects: Clear or apply effects when waking up through the letmesleep:wake_up_effects mob effect data map and the letmesleep:cleared_when_waking_up mob effect tag.
  • 🧩 Data Driven Compatibility: Control special behavior through tags such as letmesleep:never_prevents_player_rest and letmesleep:no_sleeping_interruption for seamless mod support.

⏩ INSTALLATION OPTIONAL ON CLIENT & REQUIRED ON SERVER

⏩ REQUIRES PUZZLES LIB TO BE INSTALLED (FABRIC & NEOFORGE)

⏩ REQUIRES FABRIC API TO BE INSTALLED (FABRIC)

⏩ REQUIRES FORGE CONFIG API PORT TO BE INSTALLED (FABRIC)

If available for a mod, configuration is possible directly from in-game using the mod menu (requires Mod Menu by Prospector to be installed on Fabric).

For manual configuration using an external text editor all files are found at .minecraft/config, named as MOD_ID-client.toml, MOD_ID-common.toml, or MOD_ID-server.toml, depending on the type of config. Not all types might exist for a mod, if any at all.

🌟 Thanks to VikeStep and their now outdated Nearby Mob Finder mod for inspiring the glowing feature.

title: The Game Crasher
description: Instantly crash minecraft with 1 command on any PC! (Not a lag crash)
body:
## Crash minecraft with only 1 command instantly, on any PC
Have you ever thought of purposefully crashing minecraft with 1 command, for a cool effect for horror maps or just to prank your friends? Well this is a simple datapack I made to achieve this.

Run this command to crash the game:
### `/function ant:crash`
---
The crash is **not** making lags on purpose or out of memory stuff, it is reusable, so you can safely join your world again after a crash and everything will *probably* be fine.

This datapack was made by using a worldgen bug [MC-264777](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-264777), so the function just loads a chunk in a custom void dimension that has noise settings height defined bigger than the max build height. The datapack can be installed both during world creation and to an existing world, but you need to re-enter your world 1 time after installing in an existing already loaded world, `/reload` won't work. Before entering a world with this datapack you will see a warning.

Keep in mind that because it's a **bug**, this can be fixed in future versions, and any mod may fix the crash or make things even worse. For example `Concurrent Chunk Management Engine` mod will break the datapack.

**I strongly recommend to make backups of your important worlds before installing this datapack to them, because even tho my tests show that everything is fine, every type of crash may damage your world.**

title: Inertia!
description: A camera overhaul with camera smoothing, vertical motion smoothing and tools to reduce motion sickness!
body:
# Inertia! ### Fluid Camera & Motion Overhaul [![Mod Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/Version-1.0.0-gold?style=for-the-badge)](https://modrinth.com/mod/inertia) [![Fabric](https://img.shields.io/badge/Loader-Fabric-beige?style=for-the-badge&logo=fabric)](https://fabricmc.net/) **Bring fluidity and comfort to Minecraft.** *Remove the rigid stiffness of vanilla movement and eliminate motion sickness.*
--- ## 🌊 What is Inertia? Inertia! replaces the rigid, snapping camera of vanilla Minecraft with a silky-smooth, responsive system. **It removes the harsh micro-stutters and "stair-stepping" of vanilla movement, replacing them with fluid transitions.** It operates on a simple philosophy: *Gameplay should feel comfortable, not jarring.* - Hate the screen snapping when walking up stairs? **Smooth it out.** - Tired of micro-jitters from your mouse? **Filter the noise.** - Suffer from motion sickness? **Stabilize your view.** Designed with accessibility in mind, Inertia! makes Minecraft feel modern and fluid, giving you full control over how your camera handles. --- ## 🎥 Key Features Inertia! polishes the rough edges of the game engine without sacrificing the precision you need for gameplay. ### ☁️ Vertical Smoothing * **No More Stair-Stepping:** The camera glides smoothly when walking up blocks, stairs, and slabs, removing the rapid "snap" effect that causes eye strain. * **Softened Descents:** Falling feels less abrupt. The camera transitions smoothly downward, removing the jarring visual disconnect of rapid height changes. * **Cushioned Landings:** Instead of snapping instantly to the ground, the camera stabilizes gently upon landing, making movement feel continuous rather than jagged. ### 🖱️ Input Polish * **Fluid Aim:** Mouse movement is interpolated independently of the render rotation. * **Jitter Elimination:** This eliminates the "stepping" feel of high-DPI mice and low framerates while ensuring your aim remains accurate. * **Crosshair Sync:** Unlike cinematic cameras that misalign your aim, Inertia! ensures your crosshair always interacts with the block you are looking at. ### 🤢 Motion Sickness Relief * **Bobbing Separation:** Specifically designed tools allow you to decouple head bobbing (the camera shake) from hand bobbing (the walking animation). * **Jagged Terrain:** A custom smoothing curve removes the harsh camera snaps when navigating rough terrain. --- ## ⚙️ Configuration & Presets Inertia! is fully configurable via **Mod Menu**. Choose from tuned presets or customize every value to your liking. ### ☁️ Smooth (Recommended) Optimized for a fluid, modern feel. It eliminates micro-jitters and smooths out the harsh "stair-stepping" of vanilla movement. Perfect for players prone to motion sickness. ### 🍦 Vanilla Returns the camera to standard Minecraft behavior while keeping the mod active, allowing you to selectively enable specific features like "Bobbing Separation" manually. ### 🔧 Custom Want something specific? Inertia! gives you full control. Tweak vertical rise/fall speeds, mouse smoothing, and bobbing logic to create your perfect setup. --- ## 🔧 Technical Details Inertia! is built to be lightweight and compatible with modern rendering mods. * **Client-Side Only:** This mod is purely visual. You can use it on any server without it needing to be installed on the backend. * **Dependencies:** Requires **Fabric API**. **Mod Menu** is highly recommended to access the settings. * **Compatibility:** Fully compatible with Sodium and Iris.

body:
![Authentic Adventure Lite logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BlueStaggo/authadvlite/1.3.2/logo.png)

Minecraft Authentic Adventure Lite is a minimalistic mod for Minecraft 1.3.2 to 1.8.9 that tweaks primary aspects to be more Beta-esque. It is a smaller version of the [Authentic Adventure](https://github.com/BlueStaggo/AuthenticAdventure) mod which features many more customisation options and gameplay tweaks.

## Installation
Authentic Adventure Lite makes use of the [Ornithe project](https://ornithemc.net/) to allow for easy porting between versions as well as compatibility with other mods. Simply install Ornithe then download the respective version of the mod and move it to your mods folder. Ornithe standard libraries are not required.

## Features
- Overhauled world generation, making it more hilly and Beta-esque (mostly identical to the original mod)
- Reworked hunger system (hunger only decreases with sprinting, starvation has been removed and food directly heals health)
- Restored old passive mob spawning
- Enchantments cost one quarter of the level requirement 
- Ability to safely upgrade to later Minecraft versions

## Extra Features (Full Mod)
*These features can be found in the full version of the mod for 1.2.5*
- Plenty of customisation options for world generation, gameplay and visuals to fine tune your experience
- New classic mode for a truly beta-like experience
- Extra challenging hardcore mode
- Plenty of minor gameplay and visual tweaks

body:
# Programmer Art Updated

Stemming from my personal dissatisfaction with Mojang's handling of the "Programmer Art" resource pack, and my personal dislike of quite a few of Minecraft's old textures, the goal of this pack is to give "old" textures to blocks that never had them, whilst also updating textures that haven't held up as well over the years. The designs of certain blocks (meaning not just the texture but the underlying design) have also been changed and adapted to fit the feel and look of Minecraft's old artstyle. The project started as a small personal endeavor, originally only meant to replace the old mossy cobblestone and old netherrack texture, but has since grown into a passion project with the goal of bringing back a part of Minecraft's identity that it lost after the texture update.

## IMPORTANT!
**To properly use the pack, apply Mojang's built-in Programmer Art resource pack first, then put Programmer Art Updated above it.**

title: Low Armor Notifier
description: Notifies you when your armour is about to break
body:
## The Mod

This mod's idea is simple: it will alert you whenever your armour is about to break. It works by checking every tick if the ratio between the current durability of your armour and the max durability of your armour is less than a user-defined percent value.

It also plays a fun little sound every time this alert is triggered.

You do not need any other mods to run this one, it is completely independent of any other libraries.

## How can I change the settings of the mod?

You can do this by typing `/armornotifications` in chat and hitting enter. This will bring you to the configuration screen, where you can change the settings you want and hit "done" when you're, well, done.

## Credits

A huge thanks goes out to Jan for helping me with the custom config screen, whose discord server can be found [here](https://discord.gg/zurPghb8Pv). Also thanks to lwes_ (discord handle: lwes_) for helping me with the icon for the mod.

AutoClutch is a quality-of-life mod designed to assist with water bucket clutching. It helps reduce missed placements by triggering your bucket at the right moment during a fall, improving consistency without changing core gameplay mechanics.

AutoClutch monitors your fall state and assists with water bucket placement when a fall that could cause damage is detected. The timing is configurable and includes slight variation to keep behavior natural and consistent with normal gameplay.

title: NotzScoreboard
description: A multi scoreboard plugin for staff, ranks and VIPs with multi-line system and animation support. Fully customizable.
body:
##### **NotzPlugins** # # NotzScoreboard is a complete and fully customizable scoreboard plugin that features: support for multiple simultaneous scoreboards; multiline and animation support; ViaVersion support for legacy players in 1.20/1.21 servers; its own placeholders and PlaceholderAPI; database via MySQL or SQLite and dynamic updating for greater efficiency.
## Information ### Scoreboards The plugin has dynamic scoreboards that only update the placeholders inserted in each line, without having to reload the scoreboard completely! It also contains multiple customization commands so that they can be created and modified directly from the server without having to mess with the files. ### Groups The scoreboards are separated by groups and pre-programmed so that it is possible to view players from other groups (and even from the same group) on your scoreboard or from the group itself on other scoreboards. ### Templates It also has a system of templates that can be created in the plugin's configuration file and set through the game using them as Header, Footer or the main template, thus allowing greater customization and standardization of each scoreboard. ### Placeholders You can choose to use dynamic placeholders from other plugins via the PlaceholderAPI or your own static placeholders that can be created via the plugin's configuration file. ### Color codes The plugin allows you to use the old color code system and short color codes instead of creating long strings in every scoreboard line or in messages sent to players. (v4 only) ### Tip For questions or issues: [Discord @Gago32](https://discord.com/users/258701013198831617)
## Scoreboard Demo
### Player example with staff on and off

### Helper and Trial example
Show

### Mod and Admin example
Show

### Manager and Owner example
Show

## Scoreboard system (v4 only) ### Multiline separator: `--` Use `--` or more hyphens to distinguish lines. ### Prefix and Suffix line separators: `Placeholder` (the suffix), `:` (separate and keeps the ":"), `::` (only separates). ### Placeholder system It doesn't matter if you put a placeholder with `{}` or `%%`!\ The `:` in placeholders defines a default message if the placeholder doesn't exist. ### Note: Player clients in versions <1.20.3 have short lines, so the max lenght for an area in a scoreboard line (prefix, entry and suffix) is 16 chars each, making the prefix area (before a 'placeholder' or ':') only 32 chars long (counting the color codes §/&).
Example ```yml templates: - player: - '' - '⧽ {player_displayname}' - '' - '⎧ {rank}' - '⎩ {status_rankup}' - '' - '⎧ Money: {money:0.0}' - '--⎩ Cash&f: {cash:0c}' # same line, but it will - '--⎩ Tokens&f: {tokens:0t}' # alternate every X seconds - '' - '⎧ Clan: {simpleclans_clan:No clan}' - '⎩ KDR: {simpleclans_kdr:0.0}' ```

## Custom color code system (v4 only) ### Legacy color codes Use `&` along with any legacy color code.\ Example: `&b` (Old color AQUA). ### Gradient with old color codes Use `&g` along with any legacy color code.\ Example: `&g2b` (Gradient from GREEN to AQUA). ### Gradient with hexadecimal colors Use `&g[_color1_:_color..._]` along with the hexadecimal color, whether short (#f0f) or long (#ff00ff).\ Example: `&g[#fff:#000]` (Gradient from WHITE to BLACK). ### Pride colors Use `&p` alone or `&p[_flag_]` together with any [pride flag name](https://docs.papermc.io/adventure/minimessage/format/#pride).\ Example: `&p[bi]` (Bi flag gradient). ### Rainbow Use `&!` alone or together with [! or phase](https://docs.papermc.io/adventure/minimessage/format/#rainbow).\ Example: `&!` (Normal rainbow).\ Example: `&!!` (Inverted rainbow).\ Example: `&!2` (Rainbow phase 2).\ Example: `&!!2` (Inverted rainbow and phase 2). ### Chat event Use `&&_action_[_value_](_message_)` with any supported action: [copy, url, run, sug|suggest](https://docs.papermc.io/adventure/minimessage/format/#click)\ [hover](https://docs.papermc.io/adventure/minimessage/format/#hover)\ Example: `&&hover[Boooo!](Hover over this message to see something.)` (Display a message on hover).\ Example: `&©[You copied me!](Click here to copy something.)` (Copies a message).\ Example: `&&run[/tutorial](Click here to run the tutorial!)` (Executes a command).\ Example: `&&sug[/bc yipeee](Click here to be happy!)` (Suggests a command). ### End color code Use `&.` to terminate a color code (the '&.' will be removed from the message). It will also be terminated when another color code begins (auto detects another `&`).
## Dependencies - PlaceholderAPI (Optional) - ViaVersion (Optional) (v4 only)
## Placeholders | Placeholder | Description | |:-----------:|-------------| |`{money}` | Player money straight from Vault and formmated by NotzAPI. [PlaceholderAPI-Vault]| |`{staff}` | Get the nick of one of the online players in the visible groups for that group.| |`{supstaff}` | Same thing as {staff}, but returns an alternative message if there is no online player in the visible groups for that group.| |`{staff_list}` | Number of online players in the visible groups for that group.| |`{staff_'group'}` | Get one of the players in that group.| |`{'group'_list}` | Gets the number of online players in that group.|
## Permissions - `notzscoreboard.admin` - Enables the player to use the /notzsb admin command.
## Commands ### `/notzsb` - `create` \ \ (header) (template) (footer) - Creates the scoreboard with the option of already setting the templates. - `delete` \ - Deletes a scoreboard. - `list` - Lists all the scoreboards created. - `players` - Lists all registered players and their respective scoreboards. - `reset` \ - Resets the player's scoreboard to the default scoreboard. - `set` \ - Sets the scoreboard itself. - `update` - Updates all scoreboards. - `` - `addplayer` - Adds a player to the scoreboard. - `addgroup` - Adds a group to the scoreboard's VisibleGroups. - `clearheader` - Clears the scoreboard header. - `clearfooter` - Clears the footer of the scoreboard. - `cleartemplate` - Clears the scoreboard template. - `pause` (minutes) - Pause the scoreboard update for X minutes (by default it is paused for 1 minute). - `players` - View the players registered on the scoreboard. - `remplayer` \ - Remove a player from the scoreboard. - `remgroup` \ - Remove a VisibleGroups group from the scoreboard - `setcolor` \ - Sets a new color for the scoreboard. - `setdisplay` \ - Sets a new display on the scoreboard. - `setheader` \

title: Easy Spawner Control
description: Easy Spawner Control lets you right-click mob spawners with a crafted Spawner Key to instantly configure spawn speed, count, and behavior — no commands required.
body:
# Easy Spawner Control
Take ownership of every spawner on your server. Easy Spawner Control lets you decide how spawners break, what they drop, who can reconfigure them, and how fast mobs appear—all through simple server configs.

[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-JOIN-3f0f0f?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/6NJZSxXFPV) [![Ko-fi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ko--fi-SUPPORT-3f0f0f?style=for-the-badge&logo=kofi&logoColor=white)](https://ko-fi.com/bobotweaks) [![Fiverr](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fiverr-HIRE%20ME-3f0f0f?style=for-the-badge&logo=fiverr&logoColor=white)](https://www.fiverr.com/s/1qZlPl6)

![logo](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/41a582ff3325d363cfbf2215a8d02d99a349bc67.png)

## Core benefits for server owners

- **Granular mining rules** – Gate spawner drops behind Silk Touch, tool tiers, or flat-out disable intact drops while granting XP payouts and replacement blocks you define.
- **Spawner fragments for progression** – When intact drops are disabled, fragments with Fortune scaling provide a grindable upgrade path instead .
- **Mob-egg economy** – Per-mob egg drop chances, whitelists/blacklists, and per-player cooldowns keep powerful mobs in check while still rewarding farms.
- **Spawner Control menu** – Right-clicking a spawner (optionally gated by the Spawner Key) opens a GUI where players cycle spawn speed, mob count, and activation range presets without touching NBT tools.
- **Key-gated access & cooldowns** – Enforce keys, allow operator/Creative bypasses, and throttle menu uses per player to prevent spam.
- **Drop-in server configs** – Ships with `easy-spawner-control-world.cfg` and `easy-spawner-control-mob-eggs.cfg`, already sectioned for quick edits (egg drops, mining rules, menu access, delays, counts, activation range).

## Showcase features

1. **Spawner Mining Overhaul**

   - Require Silk Touch, enforce minimum pickaxe tiers, and decide if mined spawners become air, obsidian, or any block ID you provide.
   - Optional XP rewards and configurable fragment cooldowns add levers for your economy.

2. **Mob Egg Drops with Safety Checks**

   - Global enable toggle, default drop chance, whitelist-only mode, and per-entity overrides keep dragon/Wither eggs from sneaking in unless you authorize them.

3. **In-Game Spawner Editor**

   - Players cycle between Default/Medium/High/Extreme presets for spawn delay, mob count, and player range directly in-game.
   - Presets can be tuned server-side so “Extreme” matches your server performance budget.

4. **Spawner Key Progression**
   - Craftable item (toggleable recipe) that loses durability on use; gate menu access behind it while giving ops/Creative an optional bypass.

## Configuration snapshot

The mod auto-generates two configs:

- `easy-spawner-control-world.cfg` — covers egg drops, mining rules, menu access, recipes, spawn delays/counts, and activation ranges.
- `easy-spawner-control-mob-eggs.cfg` — per-mob egg drop overrides.

💡 Need step-by-step tuning advice? The full GitHub wiki walks through every section with tables, drop logic, and best practices: [github.com/BoboTweaks/Easy-Spawner-Control/wiki](https://github.com/BoboTweaks/Easy-Spawner-Control/wiki)

## FAQ

**Q: Do I need to edit world configs manually?**  
A: Only once—on first launch the mod writes both config files with detailed comments and sane defaults. Modify them and reload/restart to apply.

**Q: Can I disable the GUI entirely?**  
A: Yes. Set `menu.requiresKey = false` to let anyone open it, or disable the `spawner_control` menu entirely by removing the key requirement and locking spawner mining. You control every knob.

**Q: Does it conflict with other spawner mods?**  
A: As long as other mods don’t replace the vanilla spawner block entity entirely, ESC plays nicely. All logic hooks into block break/use events and the built-in BaseSpawner

---

**Need help or want to request features?**

- Documentation & guides: [GitHub Wiki](https://github.com/BoboTweaks/Easy-Spawner-Control/wiki)

---

**Feel free to suggest improvements or features in the comments!**

    event.recipes.oritech.foundry(
        'minecraft:sponge',     // Item Output
        ['minecraft:gold_ingot', 'minecraft:diamond']    // Item Input

    event.recipes.oritech.laser(
        'minecraft:sponge',     // Item Output
        'minecraft:sand'    // Item Input
    ).time(40)  //ticks

    event.recipes.oritech.atomic_forge(
        'minecraft:sponge',     // Item Output
        ['minecraft:diamond', 'minecraft:emerald', 'minecraft:gold_block']    // Item Input
    ).time(300)  //ticks

    event.recipes.oritech.particle_collision(
        'minecraft:sponge',     // Item Output

    event.recipes.oritech.refinery(

        [FluidOutput.of('minecraft:water', 500), FluidOutput.of('minecraft:lava', 250)],    // Fluid Output

    ).time(120)  //ticks

    event.recipes.oritech.cooler(
        'minecraft:sponge',    // Item Output
        [],     // Fluid Output, but it should remain empty because this machine doesn't have a fluid output.
        [],     // Item Input, but it should remain empty because this machine doesn't have a item input.
        FluidInput.of('minecraft:lava', 1000)     // Fluid Input
    ).time(60)  //ticks

        'minecraft:sponge',    // Item Output

This **resource pack** introduces 57 **unique** crosshairs to Minecraft, _giving_ _players_ a **fresh** and **customizable** experience when aiming. 57 Custom Crosshairs with different designs and styles.


## how to change the crosshair

Locate the "All Crosshairs" Folder:
Inside the resource pack go to assets\minecraft\texures\gui\sprites\hud folder, you will find a folder named "all crosshairs". This folder contains all 57 custom crosshairs.

Pick a Crosshair:
Inside the "all crosshairs" folder, you will see all the available crosshair images (each file is named something like crosshair1.png, crosshair2.png, etc.).

Select and Replace:

To change your crosshair, simply choose the one you want to use.
Copy your chosen crosshair image (e.g., crosshair1.png).
Go to the assets\minecraft\textures\gui\sprites\hud folder
Delete the existing crosshair.png file and paste your new crosshair image into this folder, renaming it to crosshair.png.
Enjoy Your New Crosshair:
Once you've replaced the crosshair, load up Minecraft or press f3+t to reload resourcepack and you'll see your new crosshair in the game

You can always change your crosshair by following these steps again and selecting a new one from the "all crosshairs" folder.
You can also edit the crosshairs to create your own designs if you’re comfortable with any image editing software.

body:
This vanilla-friendly and multiplayer-friendly data pack improves golden pickaxes, shovels, axes, and hoes and compatible with all Vanilla enchantments. They work on multiple blocks at the same time but mine much slower. The changes to golden tools keep the progression fresh but offering temporary but powerful alternatives during the mid to late game.

Golden pickaxes and shovels mine in 3x3 area. 

Axes fell entire trees and once and accelerate the decay of leaves.

Hoes till farmland and harvest fully grown crops in 3x3 area.

They are fully compatable with vanilla enchantments.

Crouching causes the tools to revert to their vanilla behavior so you can break one block at a time.

A config menu can be opened with `/function m_golden_tools:config` to disable/enable the datapack, configure the maximum logs broken by the axe (default to 160), and change the speed of leaf decay after using the axe (default to ~23x faster)

title: Black Flash
description: This is a mod which basically adds a small chance that you'll land a Super Critical Hit whenever you directly hit an opponent with any melee means.
body:
This is a mod which basically adds a small chance that you'll land a **Super Critical Hit** whenever you directly hit an opponent with any melee means. This means, any weapon but indirect sources such as TNT, throwable projectiles, arrows & etc don't apply. 

This mod is heavily inspired by the _Black Flash Mechanic from the Jujutsu Kaisen Anime & Manga_. it's essentially a mod that adds black flash to minecraft. Currently, the odds of landing a black flash cannot be tweaked and are hard coded as follows:

- 1 in 9 chance of landing a black flash bare handed
- 1 in 32 chance of landing a black flash with any other item in hand
  
Aside from that, a theme/music plays when you land a black flash with any other item (not bare handed). This mod is very small but adds a whole new mechanic for pvp. 

The black flash has a few effects. Upon landing a black flash, the user gains insane regen for 5 seconds (effectively immortal unless one shot in those 5 seconds), they also gain saturation for 2 seconds (restore a bit of hunger ASAP), they also gain the strength effect for 25 seconds. The entity that got hit by the black flash gains slowness (stun effect) such that they can barely move, for 2 seconds. A black flash also does 4 extra damage (that's 2 hearts of a fully UNARMOURED player) and deals tons of knockback.

 

Enjoy!

title: Verdant Growth
description: A spreading plant growth threatens to overtake and convert all matter in its path. Either fight it or join it!
body:
![A dirt block overgrown by deep green grass.](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/be2d5bf7ebcf7887bbf8b00246d450df13ee316d.png)

# The Verdant Growth

The **Verdant Growth** is an unstoppable plant infection that spreads across the world, consuming forests and reshaping landscapes. It expands through two primary mechanisms: strangler vines entwine and overgrow trees, and underground roots transform even deepslate into lush greenery. This relentless overgrowth introduces new resources, challenges, and dangers; survival can be difficult, but the rewards are well worth it. Players who unleash the **Verdant Growth** must be prepared—it cannot be contained easily.  

Overgrown regions offer unique materials and ingredients. Strangler-vine-covered trees yield large amounts of **Strangler Wood**, while the rarer **Heartwood** can be crafted into tools, weapons, and armor. Players may rarely find **Imbued Heartwood**, a key step in creating rapidly self-repairing equipment.  

Many other plants have distinct and useful properties: Poison Ivy can be crafted into **Poison Arrows**, **Thorn Bushes** provide materials for devious traps, and climbable **Strangler Tendrils** can be crafted into **Rope** and upgradable, throwable **Rope Coils**. Many plants serve as ingredients for powerful potions, while crops like **Cassava**, **Ube**, and **Coffee** introduce unique mechanics, risks, and rewards.

Fortunately, the Verdant Growth doesn’t generate in the world naturally. Players must first locate an **Overgrown Pyramid** hidden in jungle biomes and deliberately trigger its release. Once it is set loose, all players in the world will receive an advancement notification—marking the start of a slow spread that will consume and transform the world.

title: Command Safety
description: Warns the player when running potentially dangerous commands ('/kill @e' etc).
body:
# Command Safety Mod

Have you ever accidentally killed all entities in your world with a single command? Or maybe you've cleared all the scores of a player when you didn't mean to?

This mod helps you avoid such mishaps, by requiring the player to **confirm commands** that have the potential to break a lot of things.

Very useful when working on large projects, especially when multiple people (*that potentially have less experience with commands*) are involved.

-------

### The commands & the conditions of when they require confirmation:
- `/fill`, `/clone`
    - When selecting an area of more than 10 000 blocks.
- `/execute`, `/kill`, `/effect`, `/tp`, `/teleport`, `/give`, `/clear`, `/gamemode`
    - When affecting more than 50 entities (players, ravagers, item frames).
    - When affecting more than 25 living entities (players, ravagers, ...).
    - When affecting more than 1 player.
- `/scoreboard`
    - When affecting more than 50 score holders (players / entities).
    - When using the `/scoreboard players reset ..` command without selecting an objective.

![Example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mat0u5/CommandSafety/7ecd51894c579dca09e2a8e346514828c558ea52/images/example.png)

-------

### Config:

**You can use the `/confimcmd config` command to change the limits of when commands require confirmation**, or you can also modify the config files themselves (*./config/confirmcommand.properties*).


### `/confirmcmd`
- `/confirmcmd config <name>` - Gets the value of a config.
- `/confirmcmd config <name> <value>` - Sets the value of a config.

Possible values for `<name>` are: *max_blocks, max_players, max_living_entities, max_entities, max_score_holders*

# **Description:**



Apothecary is a potion expansion designed to introduce a diverse array of potion effects that enhance both utility, combat and much more. With many new beneficial and harmful effects included this mod offers a comprehensive selection of potions tailored to meet your needs and to make the game more challenging if need be, with it also including some potions for existing vanilla effects as well. While also including some overall potion related features such as potion effect descriptions or world events.



This mod comes with extensive configurability so you can customize potions/effects your liking.

As of now this mod adds 25 new effects

**Effects:**

<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

**Positive Effects: **

Iron Skin - Provides +4 Armor points


Diamond Skin - Provides +4 Armor toughness


Archery - Increases arrow damage by +3


Wrath - Increases all damage dealt by +10%


Flight - Grants creative flight


Reach - Increases reach by +1


Repairing - Repairs items in inventory at random intervals


Magic Power - Increases magic damage by +10%


Mana Regeneration - Increases mana regeneration by +25% (irons spellbooks)


Thorns - Reflect 20% of damage dealt back to attackers


Purification - Grants immunity to all harmful effects


Extension - Increases the duration of all active effects


**Negative Effects:**


Broken Armor - Reduces -4 Armor points


Ruptured Armor - Reduces -4 Armor toughness


Misfire - Decreases arrow damage by -4


Feeble - Decreases damage dealt by -10%


Vunerable - Increases damage taken by -20%


Magic Drain - Decreases magic damage by -10%


Magic Exhaustion - Decreases mana regeneration by -25% (irons spellbooks)


Confusion - Inverts controls


Corruption - Grants immunity to all beneficial effects


Burning - Sets you ablaze with fire doing more damage per level


Shocked - Decreases movement speed by -50%


Reversion - Decreases the duration of all active effects


**Vanilla Potions:**


Health Boost


Wither


Luck (recipe)


Resistance

</details>



Apothecary also enhances the game with dynamic world events that make effects more interactive, As going about playing the game you could get inflicted with a dangerous negative effect or a positive one. These events can inflict various effects, adding an exciting layer of unpredictability to gameplay.


**World Events:**


<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

Vanilla Events:

Broken armor effect can be inflicted by explosions when wearing armor

Ruptured armor effect can be inflicted by explosions when wearing armor and the damage of the explosion reaches a certain amount, also applied by piglin brutes

Direct lightning strikes can inflict the shocked effect

Any mob attack can inflict the feeble effect very rarely

Blazes can occasionally inflict the burning effect for a short time

Illusioners can inflict the confusion effect rarely

Allows witches to throw many new potions added by this mod when attacking a player


Compat Events:

Necromancers can inflict mana exaustion and magic drain (ironsspellbooks)

Blood can inflict indolence (biomesoplenty)

Acid can inflict corrosion (alexscaves)

</details>



World event features will be expanded upon


Also adds a few potion related features that should exist in minecraft (all configurable)


Adds an option to make potions have an enchanted glow (disabled by default)


Adds an option to change max potion stack size (vanilla stack size by default)


Adds an option to enable potion description tooltips to display what the effect does (disabled by default)

title: Yeth's TPA
description: An ultra-compatible, functional, and stable TPA mod
body:
**Yeth's TPA is a Teletransportation Accept mod for Minecraft designed to be compatible, stable, and sufficient.**

## Commands
- **/tpa <target>** Sends a TPA request to a user
- **/tpa accept <target>** Accepts a TPA request from a user
- **/tpa <target> here** Sends a TPA Here request to a user
- **/tpa cancel** Cancels an outgoing TPA request
- **/tpa ignore <player>** Ignores a player from making TPA requests
- **/tpa help** Sends a list of all commands
- **/tpa disable** Disables TPA requests from being sent to you
- **/tpa enable** Enables TPA requests to be sent to you
- **/tpa setting <setting> <value>** Configures settings in TPA

## Features
- Automatic expiry of TPA requests
- TP delay w/ countdown
- Multiple request handling
- Permissions for server owners
- Anti-TPA-traps

## Support
Yeth's TPA supports the following mod loaders:
- Fabric
- Neoforge
- Forge
- Quilt
- Legacy Fabric
- Babric
- Ornithe
- BTA
- LiteLoader

For Minecraft versions 1.7.2 - 26.1.2

This modpack is designed for players on the MineZ server hosted by Shotbow. Its goal is to provide optimizations for smoother gameplay and enhance the experience with specially tailored mods and configurations.

## What’s included in the modpack?
1. Game Optimization:
The modpack includes performance-boosting tools such as Sodium, and other optimization mods, enhancing the game’s performance across a wide range of hardware. With these optimizations, gameplay remains smooth even during intense interactions and large-scale exploration.

2. Minimap with Marked Locations:
This modpack integrates a custom minimap (Xaero’s Minimap and Xaero’s Worldmap), specifically configured for MineZ gameplay. Key locations, such as towns, outposts, shrines, and hidden resource spots, are marked on the map. Each location is carefully labeled to help players navigate the MineZ world and locate critical points, shelters, and important resource areas.
**Most locations are already marked, if any are missing please contact us. Through our discord server** [Discord Server Link](https://discord.gg/wYQx9K9eMV)

3. HUD and User Interface Improvements:
Additional mods, like EssentialGUI and BetterF3, enhance the user interface to make exploration more intuitive. Modified HUD elements give better access to critical gameplay information.

4. Visual and Audio Enhancements:
The modpack includes optimized texture and sound packs that match the atmosphere of MineZ. Textures retain the dark and immersive style of the game world, while sounds add ambiance and provide audio cues for threats or helpful spatial orientation.

5. Configurations for the MineZ Server:
All mods and settings are optimized for the shotbow.net server to ensure full compatibility and prevent any synchronization or stability issues. Everything is designed to maximize and enhance the experience of exploring and surviving in the MineZ world.
