title: MultiGolem
description: This project adds the ability to create new golems out of Lapis, Copper, Gold, Redstone, Emerald, Diamond, and Netherite blocks that have special abilities beyond the basic Iron Golem
body:
# MultiGolem

## Features

- Adds eight Iron Golem variants: Copper, Redstone, Gold, Lapis, Emerald, Diamond, Netherite, and Zombie.
- Server-side functional: vanilla clients can connect to a server running MultiGolem with no mod installed.
- Build variants with the vanilla iron-golem T-shape using copper, redstone, gold, lapis, emerald, diamond, netherite, or mossy cobblestone body blocks. Copper Iron Golems preserve fresh, exposed, weathered, oxidized, and waxed copper states with matching textures.
- Marked vanilla iron golem spawn eggs for Copper, Redstone, Gold, Lapis, Emerald, Diamond, Netherite, and Zombie variants.
- Each variant has its own default stats and role: Copper is lighter than vanilla, Redstone trades raw strength for emergency-control effects, Lapis is fragile anti-magic support, and Netherite is the durable endgame bruiser.
- Heal each variant with its matching material.
- Custom textures per variant on modded clients; vanilla clients still see regular iron golems.
- Optional ModMenu screens show client/server MultiGolem version status, active server customization values, and a Golempedia reference for golem creation, stats, drops, village spawns, and abilities.

## Special Abilities

- **Copper:** lightning strikes heal instead of damage.
- **Redstone:** overcharges at or below 25% health for attack and resistance without speed, then releases a Slowness X overload pulse on death.
- **Gold:** +75% movement speed, sprint-dust particles while moving, and sunlight-shine particles while idle outdoors.
- **Lapis:** protects nearby allied village entities from magic damage and configured harmful magical effects. Player protection is disabled by default and can be enabled by server config.
- **Emerald:** heals passively while villagers or wandering traders are nearby.
- **Diamond:** passive LOS lightning zap of nearby hostiles, on-attack lightning, and lightning immunity. Creepers are excluded by default.
- **Netherite:** immune to fire and lava damage, and ignites hit mobs for 5 seconds.
- **Zombie:** hostile corrupted golem that heals from Rotten Flesh, applies Hunger/Nausea/Poison to players, converts villagers and wandering traders into zombie villagers, fights village defenders, and stays allied with zombies and converted zombie villagers.

Cross-tier `ignored_target_types` lets server admins stop tiers from targeting categories such as creepers, players, endermen, or bosses. Copper, Redstone, Gold, Lapis, Emerald, Diamond, and Netherite ignore creepers by default to prevent collateral block damage.

## Creation Recipes

Build a T-shape (1 base, 1 center, 2 arms) out of one of:

- Copper Block, including fresh, exposed, weathered, oxidized, and waxed variants → Copper Iron Golem
- Redstone Block → Redstone Golem
- Gold Block → Gold Golem
- Lapis Block → Lapis Golem
- Emerald Block → Emerald Golem
- Diamond Block → Diamond Golem
- Netherite Block → Netherite Golem
- Mossy Cobblestone → Zombie Golem

Place a carved pumpkin on top. Iron golem recipe is unchanged from vanilla. The vanilla single-copper-block Copper Golem recipe remains vanilla-owned.

## Configuration

Edit `config/multigolem.json`, created on first server start. Server admins can tune:

- Global ingot healing with `allow_golem_healing`
- Per-tier `max_health`, `attack_damage`, and `anger_on_hit`
- Per-tier `ignored_target_types` values: `CREEPERS`, `ENDERMEN`, `PLAYERS`, `ALL_BOSSES`
- Ability settings for Copper lightning healing, Redstone overcharge/death pulse, Gold movement/particles, Lapis ward protection, Emerald healing aura, Diamond lightning targeting/cooldowns, Netherite fire immunity/ignite duration, and Zombie sickness/conversion/Rotten Flesh healing
- Golem availability with `golem_availability`, so servers can disable specific golem types or whole golem families from manual spawning and village spawning
- Zombie-villager village maintenance with `zombie_village_spawning`

Server owners can optionally control who may create, heal, use marked spawn eggs for, or configure spawners for each MultiGolem tier with LuckPerms-compatible permission nodes. The same creation permission nodes cover marked spawn egg use and marked spawn egg spawner configuration. Permissions are permissive by default, so existing servers keep their current behavior unless a permissions plugin denies a node.

See the [README configuration reference](https://github.com/TnTBass/multigolem#configuration) for the full config key and permission node list.

Existing V1 config files migrate automatically to the V2 schema, and unknown fields are preserved where possible.

## Modpacks

MultiGolem is allowed in modpacks.

## Client ModMenu Tools

Players with ModMenu installed can open MultiGolem's client-side hub to check whether their client and server MultiGolem versions match. Server owners and players can also inspect the connected server's active customization values, including variant health, attack damage, healing, ability settings, and village-spawn behavior. When not connected to a server, Golempedia and customization screens show MultiGolem's default values.

## Requirements

- Minecraft 26.2 or later compatible 26.x runtime
- Fabric build: Fabric Loader 0.19.2+ and Fabric API 0.152.2+26.2
- NeoForge build: NeoForge 26.2.0.6-beta or later compatible 26.2 runtime

## Spawn Eggs

MultiGolem adds Copper, Redstone, Gold, Lapis, Emerald, Diamond, Netherite, and Zombie Golem Spawn Egg stacks as marked vanilla iron golem spawn eggs. Unmarked vanilla iron golem spawn eggs remain vanilla-owned.

● CobbleCasino

  CobbleCasino is a feature-rich Minecraft Fabric mod for 1.21.1 that adds a fully functional casino experience to your Cobblemon server. Built as an addon for
  Cobblemon 1.7.3+, it brings classic casino games, gacha machines, a complete economy system, and custom NPC villagers — all tightly integrated with the Pokemon
   ecosystem.

  Games

  - Slot Machine — A fully animated 3-reel slot machine with configurable paylines (x1, x3, x5), adjustable bet amounts, win multipliers, and jackpot payouts.
  Features custom spinning sounds and visual effects.
  - Blackjack Table — A complete blackjack implementation with hit, stand, double down, and double-or-nothing mechanics. Play against the dealer with proper card
   evaluation, natural blackjack detection, and bust logic.
  - Gacha Machines — Four distinct gacha machine types:
    - Item Gacha Machine — Insert coins for randomized item rewards across five rarity tiers (Common, Uncommon, Rare, Ultrarare, Legendary).
    - Pokemon Gacha Machine — Insert coins to receive random Pokemon with configurable IVs, shininess, and aspects.
    - Plushies Gacha Machine — Use Primogems to collect plushie items with weighted drop rates.
    - Event Gacha Machine — Limited-time event rewards using special Event Coins.

  Economy

  - CrzCoin Integration — Full economy powered by CrzCoin, supporting deposits, withdrawals, and NPC shop purchases.
  - Casino Chips — 10 chip tiers from Basic to Netherite, each with configurable values. Deposit and withdraw at the Chip Table.
  - Bills — 14 denominations from $10 to $100M. Sneak + right-click to deposit directly into your CrzCoin wallet.
  - Wallet — A craftable item to manage your finances on the go.

  Gacha System

  - Pity System — Progressive legendary drop rate increase for gold and diamond coins. Guaranteed legendary after configurable number of uses, with automatic
  reset on pull.
  - Premier Bonus — After a set number of total coin uses, players receive a bonus Premier Ball Gachapon as a loyalty reward.
  - Fully Configurable Pools — Every item, Pokemon, weight, rarity, and drop rate is configurable through the mod's config files.

  NPC Villagers

  Eight custom casino villager professions, each with unique trades and custom textures:
  - Chip Dealer — Buy and sell casino chips
  - Cashier — Exchange bills and currency
  - Prize Dealer — Redeem prizes
  - TM Instructor — Purchase Pokemon TMs
  - Battle Gear — Buy battle-related items
  - Snackmaster — Food and consumables
  - Gacha Dealer — Purchase gacha coins
  - Banker — High-value financial services

  Building Blocks

  Decorative gold and diamond building blocks to create your casino floor: Cut blocks, bricks, tiles, pillars, stairs, slabs, walls, doors, and trapdoors in both
   gold and diamond variants.

  Additional Features

  - Leaderboards — Track top winners, biggest losses, highest single wins, and total spent across both slots and blackjack.
  - Music Discs — Four Pokemon Game Corner music discs (FireRed, HeartGold, Emerald, Platinum) to set the mood.
  - Pokemon Pins — Collectible pin items featuring iconic Pokemon like Eevee, Dratini, Ditto (6 IVs), and more.
  - Custom Sounds — Coin insertion, reel spinning, jackpot, win/lose, card dealing, and button press sound effects.
  - Admin Commands — Full suite of commands for managing gacha rates, player stats, leaderboards, spawning villagers, and clearing data.

title: Many Mooblooms
description: A unique take on the Moobloom, adding 16 new variants!
body:
(Note: This mod was originally known as _Trash's Mooblooms_.)

This mod adds **Mooblooms**, the flower cow from Minecraft Earth!

In this mod, Mooblooms make their comeback with 16 variants, one for each color found in Minecraft. Furthermore, each Moobloom grows a completely new flower on its back! The list is as follows:

- White (Thunderbloom)
- Light Gray (Bellflower)
- Gray (Silver Iris)
- Black (Withercup)
- Brown (Boat Orchid)
- Red (Trillium)
- Orange (Butterfly Weed)
- Yellow (Buttercup)
- Lime (Conbush)
- Green (Gladioli)
- Cyan (Centian)
- Light Blue (Myosotis)
- Blue (Dayflower)
- Purple (Morning Glory)
- Magenta (Butterfly Candy)
- Pink (Tropical Hibiscus)

However, not every Moobloom is found naturally. You can only find Yellow, Blue, and Red Mooblooms naturally. Most other Mooblooms can only be obtained through breeding Mooblooms to mix their colors.

Like Mooshrooms, Mooblooms can be sheared to harvest the flowers on their back. Unlike Mooshrooms, Mooblooms do not convert to Cows once sheared. Rather, they regrow their flowers 20 minutes after they're sheared.

When you right click a Moobloom with a dyeable item, the item will be dyed!

Also, bees pollinate with the help of Mooblooms. Mooblooms appreciate this and hold still while they do their thing. :)


<details>
<summary>MODPACK / DATAPACK DEVS</summary>

This mod comes with a total of **17 biome tags.**
`#trashs_mooblooms:moobloom_spawnable`, along with one tag for each color with the following formatting: `#trashs_mooblooms:<color>_moobloom_spawnable`.

Biomes in `#trashs_mooblooms:moobloom_spawnable` will attempt to spawn mooblooms.

Biomes in `#trashs_mooblooms:<color>_moobloom_spawnable` will attempt to make a moobloom that spawns in the assigned biomes a specific color. This will be randomized if there are multiple. Also, biomes in these tags are automatically added to `#trashs_mooblooms:moobloom_spawnable`. If you add a biome to `#trashs_mooblooms:moobloom_spawnable` without it being in any of the other tags, the moobloom's color will default to yellow.

There is also a block tag, `#trashs_mooblooms:moobloom_spawnable_on`. These are the blocks that mooblooms can naturally spawn on. By default, this is set to `#minecraft:animals_spawn_on`.

</details>

[![BisectHosting](https://i.imgur.com/6AzSqYg.png)](https://bisecthosting.com/ACGaming)

![](https://i.imgur.com/uayg09v.png)

body:
This datapack adds a Vampire to the Origins Mod, allowing you to play with a whole new range of abilities and weaknesses. Vampires heal rapidly, and can be incredibly strong and tough to kill. However, they can be killed, if weak enough, or with certain tools. 

This project is massively inspired by [Haema](https://modrinth.com/mod/haema) and [Bewitchment's Vampires](https://modrinth.com/mod/bewitchment).

**To summarise the abilities of the Vampire:**
- You do not need food, you can drink the blood of living mobs.
- You do not exhaust naturally, instead you constantly heal at the cost of blood.
- You are unable to be killed unless entirely out of blood, or by certain sources.
- You burn in daylight, and cannot heal when on fire.
- Wooden Stakes and Smite bypass your immortality, drain blood, and stun you. 
- Your strength and speed scale with your blood (food) level.

*This is a very basic description, and doesn't really do it much justice*

All the code in this project is my own, and the design is mostly my own, with inspiration taken from the aforementioned mods. Go check them out.

title: From The Red Pool [Origins]
description: A collection of origins that have emerged from the Red Pool.
body:
A collection of unique origins for all different playstyles. From The Red Pool is a mod that strives to create origins that are fun and unique. There are origins for everyone contained inside, from those who want their origin to have minimal involvement with their gameplay, to ones that change the very goals and methods of gameplay itself. 

Welcome to the pool, dive on in.

<details>
<summary>Hell's Gate</summary>
An evolving origin based around the concept of bloodthirsty demons and deal-making devils.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The origin starts as a hatchling, stranded in the Overworld. With low health, weakened attack power, hydrophobia, half a block tall, a weakness to smite, and hunger loss, it is truly a race to The Nether. 

You then have the choice of walking the path of devils or demons.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Those who chose demons walk a path of bloodshed. Starting with debuffs such as double exhaustion, carnivore, hydrophobia, a weakness to smite, slowed movements, and only a slight attack and armor buff, the player will be greatly rewarded for trudging onwards to their first kill (villagers) and unlocking their abilities.  

Starting from the second evolution, the player gains the ability to gain hunger from attacks and gets more and more attack damage, armor, and movement speed with each evolution. From the third evolution, the player unlocks a rage ability that consumes some of the collected souls for a buff effect that gets stronger the more they evolve.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

On the alternative devil pathway, charisma is key for this contract-centered route. This origin allows you to create demonic contracts with other players, granting them powers in exchange for their souls. Be careful, though, because if negotiations go south, devils aren't personally equipped for combat. With a permanent armor value of 0 as well as numerous other debuffs to start, devils are some of the weakest of the bunch when fighting alone. 

Devils grow greatly in power the more deals they make. Gaining health and magic resistance for each soul under their command. They also have many escape routes and fighting strategies once they've amassed their legion of contractees. With the ability to teleport to and summon contracted souls, devils are natural leaders, fighting from the backlines. 

Some souls may be a harder bargain than others, though, and that's where the tier and authority systems come into play. The higher the rank of the devil, the more contracts they have access to. Each devil is allotted a certain amount of authority to spend the way they see fit, with higher-ranking contracts costing more. Spend too much, though, and you may not have enough left to rank up.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

All routes have a nice set of extra bonuses here and there to enjoy as well, such as night vision for the higher-ranking infernal entities, fire and temperature (thermoo) resistance for all, and a litany of other powers waiting to be unlocked. What are you waiting for? Insert the key and unleash the Gates of Hell today.
</details>


<details>
<summary>Jinn</summary>

  # Jinn (Impact 2) #

A territorial ghost that remains in the spirit realm till it decides to hunt its prey.

Pros
- Aggression: Gains access to the aggression stat, which allows an entity to enter into hunting mode, gaining buffs. Gains stacks of aggression in the dark and when hitting living entities.

Mixed
- Undead: You're an undead
- Flicker: Flash in and out of existence

Con
- Hunt: When not hunting, receive weakness 4

Abilities
- [Primary] Teleport to a point within 10 blocks (Doesn't work during hunt)
- [Secondary] Able to go into a 'hunt' mode that disables invisibility, grants strength 3 and resistance 2. Increases speed proportional to distance to non-undead (line of sight). Can extend the duration of the hunt through killing living entities.

_Dedicated to Cantankerouss_
</details>


<details>
<summary>Martial Artist</summary>

# Martial Artist (Impact 2) #

Body forged by blood, sweat, tears, and cheat codes.
  
Pros
- Martial Arts: Some items in the off hand cause effects when punching

<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

  - Blaze powder: Fire aspect
  - Chain: Stun (Nausea, mining fatigue, and slowness for 2 seconds)
  - Shulker box: Levitation 2 (1s)
  - Powdered Snow: Freeze
  - Zombie Head: Hunger (2s)
  - Netherite block: +5 additional damage (gives mining fatigue)
  - Pufferfish: Poison 2 and Nausea 6 (4s)
  - Brewing Stand: Random potion effect (positive or negative)
  - Glowstone block: Glowing (5s)

</details>


- Hardened Fist: +5 damage with fists
- Undefended Defense: +50% armor while not wearing armor
- Free Movement: Haste 3 when no armor and bare fist

Cons
- Martial Pride: You refuse to use a shield and you won't use your martial arts while you're wearing armor
- Tiring: Increased hunger loss
- Keto: Half benefit from non-protein items

_Dedicated to twistedassassin2_
</details>


<details>
<summary>Oppressor</summary>

# Oppressor (Unchoosable) #
An origin fit for a tyrant

Abilities (Togglable)
- [Primary] Avert Thy Eyes: Aura that gives slowness 7,  weakness 7, and mining fatigue 10 to others (10 block range)
- [Secondary] Kneel Before The King: Aura that gives darkness 3, blindness 3, and night vision 3, to others (10 block range)
- [Load] The Weightless Crown - Swim through the air
- [Jump] On The Masses - Allows you to jump mid-air.

_Dedicated to Poke097_
</details>


<details>
<summary>Rabbit</summary>

# Rabbit (Impact 1) #
Carrot muncher.

Pros
- Carrot storage: Eating carrots charges your carrot meter
- High Carotene: Night vision (toggles with [Load])

Mixed
- Prey: You have reduced health, but you're small and fast
- Special Diet: You can only eat carrots and golden carrots, but they give you more food

Abilities

- [Secondary] Replenish: Intimidate all the carrots around you into growing faster (Costs 10 carrots)

_Dedicated to kalee79_
</details>


<details>
<summary>Scorpion</summary>

  # Scorpion (Impact 2) # 

A desert creature that has developed the ability to intake poisons and make them it's own.

Pros
- Storage: Creates a poison meter that regenerates naturally
- Poison synthesis: Being poisoned makes your meter go up faster
- Light: Increased speed
- Sharp Legs: Can climb

Mixed
- Insect: Half a block tall
- Desert Body: Lose frost resistance, but gain heat resistance (Thermoo)

Cons

- Unnatural Environment: Get weakness and slowness in cold biomes

Abilities
- [Primary] Able to cycle through poisons, stronger poisons use up the poison meter more
  - None: No poison (Level 0)
  - Basic Poison (Level 1): Poison 1 (5s)
  - Sickening Poison (Level 2): Nausea 3 (5s), Weakness 2 (3s)
  - Nerve Poison (Level 3): Blindness (5s), Mining Fatigue 2 (5s), Slowness 2 (5s), Weakness 2 (5s) 
  - Paralysis Poison (Level 4): Slowness 7 (6s), Mining Fatigue 4 (3s), Weakness 5 (3s)
  - Lethal Poison (Level 5): Poison 3 (3s), Wither 5 (3s)

_Dedicated to AmuTheDemon_
</details>



<details>
<summary>Wabbajack</summary>

  # Wabbajack (Impact 3) #

The gambler's dream, only to be used by the insane.

Mixed
- Gambler's Body: You will have random properties applied to you every 5 minutes

Abilities
- [Primary] Roulette: Give yourself and an opponent you're looking at a random potion effect, good or bad

_Dedicated to OinglyBoingly_
</details>


<details>
<summary>Zookeeper</summary>

  # Zookeeper (Impact 1) #

You have dedicated your life to the preservation and protection of all species of creature.

Pro
- Treatment: Heal your tamed creature when you hit them (Damage is not dealt)

Cons
- Vegetarian: You throw up any meat you consume.
- Pacifist: -2 hearts, 0.8x attack damage

Abilities
- [Primary] Relocate: Teleport tagged entities to a point within range, while nearby a respawn anchor.
  - [Right click] Bag n' Tag- Tag a non-player/undead entity to bind them for teleportation.
- [Secondary] Nuturing Gaze: Tame the creature you are looking at.

_Dedicated to Kittlyy_
</details>


<details>
<summary>Extra Information</summary>

You can disable any of the origins or powers through the config folder for the pack {config>origins_server}

You can 'break' a contractor (removing all their contracts and make them unable to form new ones) by running the command [/power revoke (playername) redpool:hellsgate/pro/devil/contract/grants/contract_unlock]. 
It is important to note that this cannot be easily undone.

You can pick oppressor with the command /origin set [playername] origins:origin redpool:one-offs/oppressor

</details>

title: Lore Accurate Craftable Totem of Undying
description: As the title suggests this mod allows you to craft a totem of undying. Now with proper lore accuracy.
body:
This mod allows the player to craft totems of undying on their own without needing to hunt down those pesky illagers. Whilst most craftable totem mods would require the player to have to obtain an endgame item to craft one this one substitutes that requirement with a seemingly hilariously easy to obtain yet lore accurate item. That item being lapis lazuli specifically a block of lapis lazuli along with 4 blocks of gold and 2 blocks of emeralds. You see the difficulty for crafting the totem in this mod isn't the fact that you have to kill a boss for it but the fact that you have to spend a lot of time in the mines gathering the materials to craft it which is why I feel that this mod is "perfectly balanced."


TL;DR very simple to get(potentially tedious)
Recipe: 4x Gold Block, 2x Emerald Block, 1x Lapis Lazuli Block.
Crafting goes: Emerald top left, Gold top middle, Emerald top right, Gold middle left, Lapis middle middle, Gold middle right, Empty bottom left, Gold bottom middle, Empty bottom right.

title: Flashback Settings
description: Adds missing settings to the Flashback mod (Fabric) - starting with choosing the replay save folder. Anonymous opt-out telemetry.
body:
# Flashback Settings

A small **Fabric client mod** that adds missing settings to Moulberry's
[Flashback](https://modrinth.com/mod/flashback) mod.

## ⭐ First feature: choose where replays are saved

By default, Flashback saves replays in `.minecraft/flashback/replays`. Flashback Settings lets you
redirect that location to any folder you want (another drive, a shared folder, a dedicated SSD for
editing, etc.).

### How to use
1. Install Fabric Loader, **Flashback**, and Flashback Settings in `.minecraft/mods`.
2. Launch the game once: the file `config/flashbacksettings.json` is created.
3. Set your path in `settings.replay_folder`, then restart:

```json
{
  "telemetry": true,
  "settings": { "replay_folder": "D:/Replays/Minecraft" }
}
```

Leave it empty to fall back to Flashback's default folder. *(An in-game config menu is planned.)*

## Compatibility
- **Loader:** Fabric only (Flashback is Fabric-exclusive).
- **Minecraft versions:** 1.21.11 (26.1.x coming soon).
- **Required dependency:** [Flashback](https://modrinth.com/mod/flashback).

## How it works
A Mixin intercepts `com.moulberry.flashback.Flashback#getReplayFolder()` and returns the configured
folder when one is set; otherwise Flashback's default behavior is kept.

## Telemetry
Anonymous usage statistics are **enabled by default** (EU region) to track adoption and versions in
use. They can be **turned off** in three ways: `"telemetry": false` in the config file,
the JVM flag `-Dflashbacksettings.telemetry=false`, or automatically in a development environment.
No IP address or geolocation is collected; an anonymous, persistent `install_id` is used as the
identifier.

## License
PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 — source-available, non-commercial use.

---

✨ WHY CHOOSE ROSERP?

RoseRP is a plugin for the effortless management of resource packs in Minecraft. It allows you to zip a resource pack using the **`/roserp zip`** command and automatically host it on the server, eliminating the need to manually host files on cloud storage like Dropbox or Google Drive. Simply use **`/roserp texture`** to apply the server-generated resource pack to players instantly! ---

⚡ PLUGIN FEATURES

* **Auto-Hosting:** Hosts the resource pack directly on your server. * **Multi-Version:** Seamless compatibility with multiple versions. * **Integrations:** Works with BetterHUD, ItemsAdder, Oraxen, and more. * **Security:** Protects resource packs from being unpacked. * **Optimization:** Asynchronous resource pack building & Automatic SHA1 hash generation. * **Delivery:** Automatic delivery to players on login. Supports multiple packs per player (1.20.3+) and forced installation (1.17+). * **Customization:** Displays custom messages on the prompt screen and allows resetting via command. ---

🛠️ HOW IT WORKS & SETUP

**How Does Resource Pack Hosting Work?** The plugin sets up a small, dedicated web server on a different port to host the resource packs. This bypasses common cloud-storage limits and saves time. Running this web server does **not** impact your server’s performance. **How to Upload a Resource Pack:** * **Place the contents:** Copy your resource pack files and folders into the designated folder on your server. * **Customize configuration:** Open *config.yml* and ensure the resource pack folder name matches the one specified in the config. * **Apply:** Use the plugin commands to package and apply your resource pack! **Configuration Instructions:** Open a port (e.g., **8443**) on your server for the resource pack. You can consult your hosting provider for guidance. Enter this open port in the plugin configuration. *Note: Changing the port requires a full server restart (reloading the plugin is not enough).* ---

title: RichLocalTextLib
description: Rich text support for translations
body:
# RichLokalТекстLib


RichLocalText is a library that allows modders and pack-makers to use translated rich text.  
Easily add font styles and colors anywhere without code! 

# Installation
Drop the .jar into the /mods folder, and enjoy rich localization text.  
Requires no other dependencies.

\*_resourcepack utilizing the_ **Rich**™ Lokal™ ***Текст***™ _Capabilities™ not included._

# Usage
Use /tellraw-like format in language files.  
When overriding a string that has format placeholders use {"index":n} instead;

Example, changing the default chat text format:
```
//en_us.json
{
  "chat.type.text": 
  [
    "", 
    {"text":"A mysterious stranger known only as <", "color": "gray"},
    {"index":0, "obfuscated": true},
    {"text":"> uttered: \"", "color": "gray"},
    {"index":1},
    {"text":"\"", "color": "gray"}
  ]
}
```
**N.B.:** If your first text component is styled, all components after it will inherit its style. This is a Minecraft quirk that we are not going to fix.


This results in text like this:  
![screenshot of rich text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BasiqueEvangelist/RichLocalTextLib/main/media/chat-example.png)

##  **Description:**
This datapack adds SCP-3008, otherwise known as the infinite Ikea to minecraft.  SCP-3008 is, just as the name suggests, an Ikea that goes on forever.  The SCP is inhabited by strange faceless beings known as "Staff" which become aggressive at night.  Will you be able to survive and find an exit?
## **Features:**
-A new dimension with a day/night cycle

-A new mob

-A new structure in the overworld

-New advancements

## **Getting Started:**
-Find the new "Ikea" structure spawning in the plains and click the doors to enter the new dimension.

-Explore the infinite Ikea and search for supplies, you may even find villagers with custom trades.

-Set up shelter before nightfall as this is when the Staff become aggressive, you may try to sleep but it's useless as the night cannot be skipped.

-Find an exit to escape the Ikea, but be quick as these tend to move at random.

-(Bonus Tip): The Staff can also break blocks.

## **Special Thanks:**
Thanks to MrCube6 for the infinite generation (I'm too dumb to make something like that myself lol)

## **WARNING:**
In order for this to work properly your render distance must be set to 15 in the custom dimension, anything more and you'll see into the void, anything less and it won't generate!

title: Glowing Mobs
description: Glowing Mobs Pack adds bright glow effects to every Minecraft mob, improving visibility and giving the game a more colorful, magical look.
body:
# Glowing Mobs Pack
#### It enhances every Minecraft mob with soft, vibrant glow effects that make creatures stand out in caves, at night, and across long distances. Each mob keeps its original vanilla texture but gains emissive highlights that improve visibility and add a colorful, magical atmosphere. The glow system uses emissive texture maps powered by ETF, allowing the world to feel brighter and more alive without altering gameplay. The pack is lightweight, fully client-side, and compatible with most resource packs that don’t edit the same mob textures.
![Glowing mobs](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/zcfiGW7H/images/fbfeaec6057463d405b54c616c137f201209b8de.png)
# Features
- Emissive glow effects for all vanilla mobs  
- Soft, colorful lighting that boosts world atmosphere  
- Improved visibility in dark areas and nighttime exploration  
- Vanilla-faithful textures with enhanced glow details  
- Visual-only upgrade with no gameplay changes  
- Lightweight and optimized for smooth performance  
- Compatible with most texture packs that do not replace mob textures  
  
# Dependencies
- **Entity Texture Features (ETF)** is required  
- All glow effects rely on ETF’s emissive texture system  
- Without ETF installed, mobs will appear with normal vanilla textures  
- Works with any client or mod loader that supports ETF (OptiFine alternatives recommended)

Welcome to the `creative-central` page, creative-central is a plugin
that unifies the server's resource-pack, allowing other plugins to
programmatically add resources to the server's resource-pack

`creative-central` allows administrators to use multiple plugins that

Do you know [Vault](https://github.com/MilkBowl/Vault)? Vault provides an API to

- Automatically generate the server's resource-pack
- Automatically upload the resource-pack to a server or host it locally
- Automatically send the resource-pack to everyone

- **..and all the benefits from [creative](https://unnamed.team/docs/creative)**

title: TacZ Mesh Loader [TML]
description: This mod allows you to load mesh geo models created with the Meshy plugin into TacZ.
body:
![tmllogo](https://i.ibb.co/B8yzy85/tmllogo.png)


This add-on is not an official TacZ add-on; it is unofficial. Please do not report any bugs caused by this add-on to the TacZ server under any circumstances. Please report them exclusively in the comments section of this mod or on Vell's Mods info server.

Please note that Forge 1.20.1 requires the official Timeless and Classics Zero Guns, Fabric 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 require TaCZ: Refabricated, and NeoForge 1.21.1 requires the [UNOFFICIAL] TaCZ NeoForge Port as dependency mods.

- - -

**Overview**

TacZ Mesh Loader is a client-side mod that allows TacZ gun and attachment models to use poly_mesh geometry exported by the BlockBench plugin Meshy. 

By default, TacZ only supports Bedrock-format cube models. With this mod installed, gunpack creators can use polygon mesh models — smooth shapes built from triangle and quad polygons — directly in TacZ guns and attachments.

- - -

**Features**

Poly mesh support — Loads Meshy-exported poly_mesh geometry directly into TacZ's model pipeline.

Guns & attachments — Works for both gun models and attachments such as scopes and suppressors.

VBO caching — At first glance, you might think that mesh models put a strain on your computer, but this mod incorporates VBO processing, which minimizes the load even when you spawn a large number of mesh model guns at once.

- - -

**For Gunpack Creators**

-Those who want to enable VBO-

If you want to create everything with mesh models and enable VBO, first convert all cube models to mesh before exporting if you used cube models before converting to Bedrock geometry using the Meshy plug-in. Next, merge all converted mesh objects into one mesh object per bone. (You only need to merge them into one mesh object per bone, and you do not need to merge all hierarchical bone objects into one.) Failure to do this will cause rendering problems when the model is loaded by TacZMeshLoader after exporting using the Meshy plugin.


-For mixed cube and mesh models-(*VBO is not supported in the cube model.)

First, for the mesh model, be sure to merge each bone into a single mesh object as described above. Next, for the cube model, there is no need to do anything to it.

The model type can only be defined if this MOD is installed. In the JSON file used for display, simply define a new “model_type”and set it to “mesh”. Please note that the definition ‘model_type’:“mesh” is only required for the gun itself and is not necessary for attachments. Please note that even if a model consists primarily of cube models, you must define “model_type”: “mesh” if it contains even a single mesh model.


```
{
  "model_type": "mesh",
  "model": "mypack:gun/mygun_geo",
  "texture": "mypack:gun/uv/mygun",
  "animation": "mypack:mygun"
}
```

File locations and structure follow the standard TacZ gunpack format. Models should be created in BlockBench using the Meshy Plugin. You can download it directly from the blockbench plugin list.

Please note that if you use this MOD to create and release a gun pack for mesh models, you must define this MOD as a dependency.

Important Note:
At this time, the ocular object does not support mesh models and only works properly with cube models. Therefore, please do not use mesh models when using the ocular object.

- - -
**License**

GPL-3.0

- - -
**Credits**

Author: VellEagle

title: c418only
description: Removes all non-c418 ambient music and remaps every music to point to c418's music.
body:
c418only strips all non-C418 ambient music from the game and remaps those slots back to C418 tracks. That's it.

Mojang has been gradually replacing the ambient soundtrack since 1.16. Lena Raine, Kumi Tanioka, Aaron Cherof, Samuel Åberg. Some of them make fine music. It's just that they **don't** make Minecraft music. C418's work on Volume Alpha and Beta is one of the most distinctive soundscapes in gaming history and it deserves to play uninterrupted.

**What this does**

- Removes all non-C418 ambient/background tracks added since 1.16
- Remaps those music event slots to C418 tracks from Volume Alpha & Beta
- Music discs are completely untouched. You can still listen to your tracks you found on loot chests.
- No audio files are bundled. this mod only overrides sounds.json event mappings to redirect vanilla assets you already have

**What this doesn't do**
Nothing else. No gameplay changes, no performance impact, no config screen. It's extremely small.

**Compatibility**
Fabric - Java 1.21.x - Client-side only, works on any server

**Legal note:** No music files are included or redistributed. This mod remaps vanilla sound event keys only. All audio remains Mojang's assets on your own installation.

**PS:** I added the source code as a zip file, so you can check it out yourself. I also provided a GitHub link.

Or to put it in more technical terms, the plugin can only access files or folder whose absolute path starts with the absolute path to the server folder. Furthermore, CogWorks is still in alpha, so there will be bugs. If you find any please report them in #bug-reports in [discord](https://discord.gg/3CC6kVcdQH). We will listen to any feedback given & we greatly appreciate it. ## General Info: ### Incompatibilities: There may be some issues with messages getting cancelled when interacting with the CogWorks chat messages, if a plugin that alters chat messages is also installed. An example of this would be any of the no chart report plugins.
If you are the author of one of these plugins or have any idea on how to resolve this issue please contact tye though [discord](https://discord.gg/3CC6kVcdQH). ### Download: The latest public version of the plugin will always be available on [Modrinth](https://modrinth.com/plugin/file-manager) & [GitHub](https://github.com/Mapty231/CogWorks/releases). Or you can join on the [discord](https://discord.gg/3CC6kVcdQH) to see if there are any snapshot builds you can mess around with! ### Commands: - "/plugin help" - §aShows a help message message. - "/plugin install " - Downloads the file from the url to the "./plugins" folder. - "/plugin search " - Uses Modrinth to search the name given and returns the results, which can be chosen from to download. - "/plugin browse" - Allows the user to search though the most popular plugins on modrinth that are compatible with your server type and install them with the press of a button. - "/plugin reload" - Forces CogWorks to rescan the "./plugins" folder. - "/plugin remove " - Disables and uninstalls the given plugin. - "/file help - Shows this message. - "/file chat - (WIP) Turns your chat into a mock command line which lets you interact with files on the server. - "/file gui - Opens an inventory that lets you interact with the files on the server visually. - "/file recover - Restores a deleted file to the given path, if no path is given then the file is restored to the server folder. ### Features: - Install jar files from the web using "/plugin install \" - Installing plugins from Modrinth using "/plugin browse" or "/plugin search \". - Will automatically install the dependencies of a plugin when downloading from Modrinth. - Will attempt to meet unmet dependencies on start up if CogWorks detects any. Disable this in the config if you have a slow connection or limited bandwidth. - Deleting plugins using the "/plugin remove \". - When deleting plugins their will be a prompt on whether to delete the plugins config folder & a prompt on whether to delete plugins that depend on the plugin that is being deleted to function. - Access a GUI file explorer with "/file". - Unique way of interacting with the plugin by being able to just type responses in chat. No commands required! - Supports permissions. - Supports "/reload". ### Permissions: - cogworks.plugin.ins.gen - Able to use the "/plugin install \" command to install a plugin from any URL. - cogworks.plugin.ins.modrinth - Able to use the "/plugin search \" & "/plugin browse" commands to install plugins from Modrinth. - cogworks.plugin.reload - Able to use the "/plugin reload" command which makes CogWorks "rescan" the "./plugins" folder for any changes. - cogworks.plugin.rm - Able to use the "/plugin remove \" command to remove plugins & their config folders. - cogworks.file.nav - Able to use the "/file" command to view files & folders, & navigate though folders. - cogworks.file.read - Able to read the content of files when using the "/file" command. - cogworks.file.edit - Able to edit the content of files when using the "/file" command. - cogworks.file.mk - Able to create new files when using the "/file" command. - cogworks.file.rm - Able to delete files when using the "/file" command. - cogworks.file.rec - Able to recover deleted files using the "/file recover" command. ### Config help: Lang: The value of this will determine which lang file CogWorks will use. If you want to help CogWorks support another language see [Translators Wanted!](#translators-wanted). To find out what values you can use, either follow the link in your config file. Or follow [this](https://github.com/Mapty231/CogWorks/tree/master/langFiles) link, select the folder corresponding to the version of CogWorks that you are using, & the file names are the available values. Just remember to not include the ".yml" when entering the file name. ShowErrorTrace: This determines if CogWorks will show error information in the console when an error occurs. This will be enabled by default until CogWorks is out of alpha & beta. If you are reporting a bug with CogWorks you will need to have this enabled when submitting a bug report. Set to "true" to enable this or "false" to disable this. Do know that this only applies to errors accounted for in the code. If the error hasn't been accounted for then a stack trace will be sent in the console regardless. ShowOpErrorSummary: When players who have op join, the number of severe errors that have happened with this plugin since last reload/restart is send to them. Set to "true" to enable this or "false" to disable this. ADR: If a plugin is missing a dependency on server start, CogWorks will try to automatically resolve the dependency by downloading it from Modrinth. If no match can be found on Modrinth then it is not attempted again. Set to "true" to enable this or "false" to disable this. It is recommended to disable this if you have a slow connection or limited bandwidth. KeepDeleted: Time: How long a deleted file should be kept until it should be deleted. The value given should use the format: {number}w for week, {number}d for day, {number}h for hour, {number}m for minute. Example: "1d3h" This would keep files for one day & three hours at most. If you don't want files to be deleted based on time, set this to "-1". Size: The max size that the restore folder can have. If it goes over this value then the oldest files will be deleted until the size is under the size specified given. If a deleted file is bigger than the specified size then it will be deleted straight away & the files already present in the restore folder will be unaffected. The value should be given in the format: {number}g for gigabytes, {n}m for megabytes, {n}k for kilobytes. Example: "100m20k" This would make sure that the restore folder never gets bigger than one-hundred Megabytes & twenty Kilobytes. If you don't want files to be deleted based on the restore folder size, set this to "-1". ### Future Plans: - Supporting downloading plugins from other websites. - Chat based file manager. - Allow to install multiple plugins at once when using a url. - Fix when using plugin install, if you enter the select number for plugin version quick enough repetitively, the plugin will install twice (only one file will still show up). - Make to try & install plugins for the correct server version if the server is updated. - Allow the sender to pass though an offset when using /plugin browse? - Send lang update messages on op join. - Allow user to exit/go back from all states. - Make lang updates required to be confirmed to go away? - Make user invulnerable whilst in "/file gui" gui. - Put char limit on file gui title, so it doesn't overflow (take chars away from start of path?). - Run ADR on plugins that are installed from a URL. ## Further reading: This will be a section containing more technical details for those who are interested, or want an introduction without having to read the code. ### On chat interaction: When using CogWorks you will probably quickly notice that it has a rather unique way of handling player interactions with commands. For example, when interacting with "/plugin search ", CogWorks will send multiple messages to the user, the ones starting with "number:" are options that can be chosen from. To select one of these options simply send "number" in chat, no "/" or any other commands required. CogWorks will block the chat message from being sent to other users. In addition, with "/plugins search " & "/plugin browse" the messages sent to you with underlined text will have hyperlinks to the content they are referring to. An example of this could be "[1: Simple Voice Chat](https://modrinth.com/mod/simple-voice-chat)", which will take you the main page on Modrinth for the Simple Voice Chat plugin. Another place that this occurs is when there are multiple valid version of a plugin, and this time the links provided will take you to the Modrinth page for that specific version of the plugin. The links will always take you to a relevant place to learn more information about the option you want to select. ### On "/plugin install \": For this command the downloaded file extension will always be set to ".jar". Also be aware that you have to get the URL to the actual file download. Not just the URL to the website that you can download the file from or the URL to info page of a plugin. For example: Correct: https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/9eGKb6K1/versions/8sbc8kD8/voicechat-bukkit-2.4.27.jar Incorrect: https://modrinth.com/plugin/simple-voice-chat/version/bukkit-2.4.27 Incorrect: https://modrinth.com/plugin/simple-voice-chat/ Incorrect: https://modrinth.com An easy way to tell if it is a file is to check if the URL ends in ".jar". However, be warned that not all plugin download links end in ".jar"! ### On "/plugin search \": For this command the query **can** contain spaces and will still be treated as a single valid search request. Furthermore, any chars that would make an invalid URL are automatically converted into the [percent-encoding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percent-encoding) that URLs use. ### On "/plugin browse": For this command it will let you (as the name suggests) browse though the most popular plugins on Modrinth that are compatible with your server type & version. Using "0" & the max value as options for "scrolling" through the list of plugins, with the "0" input scrolling you up "where applicable", & vice versa for the max number. ### On "/plugin reload": This command makes CogWorks "rescan" the "./plugins" folder for any changes made that weren't done though CogWorks. ### On "/plugin remove \": This command will only execute the delete once it has no more plugins left in the delete queue (the delete queue is just a list of plugins that need user input for options regarding the delete) to evaluate. The command works by letting you select from any plugins in the "./plugins" folder to remove (this includes plugins that didn't load successfully). If the plugin you selected has a config folder ("./plugins/") then it will give you a prompt for deleting that also. Then if there are other plugins that have the plugin you are about to delete as a dependency then there will be a prompt asking if you want to just delete this plugin anyway, delete the plugins that depend on this one, or quit. For the option to delete the plugins that depend on this one, the plugin(s) will be added to the delete queue, so the config check & the depends on check will be executed for all of the plugins you've chosen to delete. ### On "/file" or "/file gui": This command will open an inventory for the player, which allows them to navigate though the files that have a path that starts with the same path as the one the server folder is in. For an example lets say that the server jar is located in "D:\paperSever" (this also applies to linux system, I'm just using Windows file paths as an example). The files "D:\paperSever\server.properties" & "D:\paperSever\world\playerdata" are files that a user can access since they start with the same path as the server folder. However, the files "D:/taxInformation" & "C:\Program Files" can't be accessed, since they start with a path that is different from the server folder one. All the files will be represented white wool, with the item lore of "File", & all the folders will be represented by yellow wool, with the lore of "Folder". However, do be aware that the item lore text can be changed in the lang files. And the names of the items are corresponding file names. When the user clicks on a folder, the inventory will change to display the content of the folder & the same for files. To go back, simply click on the arrow. For viewing files the user can hover over the paper to see the text for a segment of that line. And they can use the tipped arrows on the top to scroll up and down in the file. The oak sign will display the line number of the top row on your screen. The book and quill lets a person search for specific phrases in the file, and for the weird character that appears when entering the search phrase, don't worry about it, it's just there so the paper isn't called "paper", it will get automatically removed. And with the spectral arrow you select a line number to go too immediately. To edit the content of a file you'll have to viewing it, then if you want to change some text that is already written, just click on the paper with the item name of the text, and an anvil will open to let you rename the text to anything you wish. To add text onto empty lines or onto the end of a line you can click on any of the empty slots that are in the same line & the anvil menu will open again and any text you put into it will get added to the line. To remove text do the same thing you would to edit text but just delete all of it inside the anvil. Clicking on the green concrete will change the inventory allowing you to create either a file or folder. After that an anvil menu will open which allows you to set the name of the file. Make sure not to enter characters that aren't allowed to be in file names! To delete a file or folder, click on the red concrete, this will put you in "delete mode". To make this clear to the user, the files will change to orange wool & the folders will change to red wool. Then just click on a file or folder to open a delete confirm menu, then click on the green concrete to delete the file or folder. If you try and delete a folder that contains files or folders within it, there will be an extra confirmation step. ### On "/file restore \ \" When files are deleted they will be stored in "{severFolder}/plugins/.data/deletePending" until the files meet the requirements to be deleted, or are restored using this command. The selected file will be restored to the restore given, if the given path is a folder then the file will be put in the folder with it's original name. If the restore path ends in a file name the file will be renamed & moved to the restore path. ### On automatic dependency resolution: Automatic dependency resolution (this will be referred to as ADR) involves CogWorks checking for any missing dependencies on start up and trying to resolve them by taking the missing plugin name (the plugin name is the name specified in the plugin.yml) and searching that up on Modrinth. It then downloads the top then plugins (into "CogWorks/.temp/ADR/") returned by Modrinth & checks if any of the plugin names of the downloaded plugins match the plugin name of the missing dependency. If one of the plugins match it wil be moved into the "./plugins" folder. The remaining plugins will be deleted. If ADR completes without errors & the dependency still isn't resolved then it won't try to resolve the dependency again. ## Translators Wanted! If you are willing to help by translating the plugin language file into any new languages (for past versions or the current version). Please join the [discord server](https://discord.gg/3CC6kVcdQH) and ping @IWantToTranslate.

title: Piglin Netherite Upgrades
description: Changes Netherite Upgrades to have a Piglin Snout symbol instead of an arrow.
body:
Why do Netherite Upgrades have an arrow on them in-world? I understand it communicates "upgrade" in game design but it does not make as much sense for immersion. Changes **Netherite Upgrades** to have a **Piglin Snout symbol** instead of an arrow. Bonus: the item is now centered too as a result (you're welcome). Since Netherite Upgrades appear to have been originally created by the Piglins (or a group that was adjacent), it seems reasonable to me that the symbol of the piglins would be fitting to appear on these templates. ## #### MintRefresh:

title: Clear Water-texture pack
description: Experience perfectly clear water in Minecraft
body: **Clear Water is a simple and family-friendly Minecraft resource pack that transforms all water into fully transparent blocks. This allows you to see underwater clearly, making exploration of oceans, rivers, and caves easier and more enjoyable. It is lightweight, requires no mods, and works with vanilla Minecraft. Perfect for players who want a clean, unobstructed underwater view without altering other game elements.**

title: SlowUT
description: Completely customize your arm swing speeds for mining, block placing, eating, and more with a clean tabbed configuration menu.
body:
SlowUT: Ultimate Arm Animation Control
SlowUT is a lightweight client-side mod that gives you total control over your player's arm swing speed. Whether you want a more cinematic feel to your gameplay or need to fine-tune animations for specific actions, SlowUT provides a professional-grade solution.

✨ Key Features:
🎯 Action-Specific Tuning: Independently adjust the swing strength for Mining, Block Placing, Eating/Drinking, XP Bottles, Ender Pearls, and End Crystals.

🛠️ Tabbed Configuration: A clean, user-friendly menu (powered by Cloth Config) featuring "Main" and "Tuning" tabs for easy navigation.

🔒 Anti-Spam Logic: Unlike basic mods, SlowUT features custom logic that keeps your animations smooth and slow, even if you are jitter-clicking or spamming items.

⚡ Master Switch: Use the "Everything Slow" toggle to instantly apply your global settings to every action in the game.

🌍 Universal Compatibility: Works on any server! Since it only affects your local animations, it is 100% client-side safe.

Requires Fabric API and Cloth Config API.

title: Improved Enchanting
description: Definitive Edition v2 for 1.21.11 Just Came out, Come here if you want a vanilla - friendly overhaul of the enchanting system, with new enchantments, and a new enchanting system.
body:
# **Improved Enchanting**

## Overview
This mod adds some new enchantments and makes them easier to understand by putting them into seperate exlusive categories, and makes less used enchantments more viable than they were before. Definitive Eddition V2.0 is OUT, and available for the latest version of the game (1.21.11), adding Elytra, Axe, and Crossbow Enchantment upgrades. I will work on making it available for the next update, and updates to come.

### Enchantment Exlusivity Rules
For all enchantments, there are 4 tiers of enchantments ("other" is not affected), primary, which is affecting all things within its perameters, secondary affects a large group of entities, like all undead mobs, the tertiary enchantments affect smaller groups of entites, like all raiders or bosses. Special is a passive ability that affects how you use the weapon, it is probally the most important enchantment of them all. Each enchantment tier is exlusive to itself, for example you can't have 2 primary enchantments, but you can have 1 primary enchantment and 1 secondary, you have to chose between the enchantments in each level.


# Armor Enchantments


<details>
<summary>Primary Armor Enchantments</summary>

## Primary Armor Enchantments
This level incldes the enchantment, protection with a few tweaks and a new enchantment, reinforced.


<details>
<summary>Protection</summary>

### Protection
This enchantment has gone through some tweaking, it only has half the normal protection that it would normally give, and is only found in the enchanting table. With full protection 4, you get 32% general damage protection

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reinforced</summary>

### Reinforced
This enchantment gives more armor points to your player, giving 1.5 total armor bars, and an extra 4 armour toughness points. The more pieces of armor you put on with this enchantment, the bigger the upgrade is. The downside to this enchantment is that it only gives protection against direct attacks, and it is only found in ancient cities.

</details>

## Secondary Armor Enchantments
Here you will find more generalised enchantments, with bigger protection rates, it is better to mix both of these two enchantments for best results.

<details>
<summary>Melee Proteciton</summary>

### Melee Protection
This enchantment gives proteciton to all direct Melee attacks, giving 6% damage reduction per level. If you have all your armor enchanted with full Melee Protection 4 and Protection 4, it gives 128% damage reduction, but the Protection rate is hard capped at 80%, but with half of your armor with Melee Protection 4 and Full Protection 4, it gives exactly 80% damage reduction to Melee attacks. You can find this enchantment in general loot, the enchanting table and villagers.

</details>


<details>
<summary>Projectile Protection</summary>

### Projectile Protection
This enchantment gives proteciton to all direct Projectile attacks, giving 6% damage reduction per level. If you have all your armor enchanted with full Projectile Protection 4 and protection 4, it gives 128% damage reduction, but the Protection rate is hard capped at 80%, but with half of your armor with Projectile Protection 4 and Full Protection 4, it gives exactly 80% damage reduction to Projectile attacks. You can find this enchantment in general loot, the enchanting table and villagers.

</details>

## Tertiary Armor Enchantments
This level of enchantments has very specific damage types that it takes care of, using blast and Fire protection to block the Incoming damage.



<details>
<summary>Fire Protection</summary>

### Fire Protection
This enchantment gives proteciton to all Fire based attacks, giving 6% damage reduction per level. If you have all your armor enchanted with full Fire Protection 4 and protection 4, it gives 128% damage reduction, but the Protection rate is hard capped at 80%, but with half of your armor with Fire Protection 4 and Full Protection 4, it gives exactly 80% damage reduction to Fire based attacks. This enchantment also shortens the time you stay on fire for. You can find this enchantment in general loot, the enchanting table and villagers.


</details>


<details>
<summary>Blast Protection</summary>

### Blast Protection
This enchantment gives proteciton to all explosion damage, giving 6% damage reduction per level. If you have all your armor enchanted with full Blast Protection 4 and protection 4, it gives 128% damage reduction, but the Protection rate is hard capped at 80%, but with half of your armor with Blast Protection 4 and Full Protection 4, it gives exactly 80% damage reduction to Explosions. This enchantment also reduces the knockback of explosives. You can find this enchantment in general loot, the enchanting table and villagers.


</details>

## Special Enchantments
This has an assortment of some special use case enchantments, i gave the chestplate two enchantments to pick from and the pants another one to pick from, so it would have the same amount of enchantments as the helmet and the boots.


<details>
<summary>Absorbing Hearts (chestplate only)</summary>

### Absorbing Hearts
This enchantment has a chance to give you absorption on hit, blocking some damage for 5 seconds. The chance for the absorption is 10% at the start, and each level above that gives 5% extra chance for you to get absorption, and at the max level of 3, you get absorption 2, rather than 1. You can only find this enchantment in The treasure loot in the shipwrecks.

</details>


<details>
<summary>Retaliate (chestplate only)</summary>

### Retaliate
This enchantment gives you a chance to get some strength on hit, dealing much more damage in the next period of time, each level increases the time you have strength by .5 seconds after the first second. Each level also increases the damage by 3 points. The chance of the chestplate giving you strength is increased from 10% by 5% every level, up to the max level of 3, where it is 20%. This enchantment is only found in the ancient city.

</details>


<details>
<summary>Dash (leggings only)</summary>

### Dash
This enchantment is still verry buggy, and is quite confusing, when you jump up or down one block, you get a small speed boost that is maintained by jumping, (Turn off FOV effects please) This speed can scale quickly if you know what you are doing. The speed is determined by the level. This enchantment is found in regular vaults in trial chambers. Removed as of definitive version 2.

</details>



</details>


# Bow Enchantments

<details>
<summary>Bow Enchantments</summary>

## Primary Bow Enchantments
As of the beta Definitive update v1, only power exists in this enchantment level, I might change this later, but only power is in this level.

<details>
<summary>Power</summary>

### Power
This enchantment is not changed from the game, it goes up to level 5, doing much more damage. This enchantment is found in random loot, villager trades and the enchanting table.

</details>


## Secondary Bow Enchantments
This level includes some vanilla enchantments, punch is here, and peircing is now available on the bow.

<details>
<summary>Punch</summary>

### Punch
This enchantment is already in the game, and has not been altered, it hits enemies further back when hit with an arrow and goes up to two levels. This enchantment is found in random loot, villager trades and the enchanting table.

</details>


<details>
<summary>Piercing</summary>

### Piercing
This enchantment has been taken from the crossbow, and has been altered to fit the bow, it goes through mobs until it hits too many or hits the floor. At level 4 it can go through 5 mobs. This enchantment is found in random loot, villager trades and the enchanting table.

</details>

## Tertiary Enchantments
Here are some new enchantments, Firestorm and Volley, alongside flame.


<details>
<summary>Volley</summary>

### Volley
This enchantment lets you shoot up to 5 arrows, in a short line, at the cost of durability. it makes it easy to deal with mass mobs in smlaller areas, on level one it lets you shoot 3 arrows, and at level 2 it lets you shoot 5. as of the definitive update v1.1, it is found in pillager outposts

</details>

<details>
<summary>Firestorm</summary>

This is a chaotic Enchantment, causing a fireball to blow up in the area that does not damage the area around it. It does some serious damage to the mobs around it. This enchantment only has one level, doing fire spreading around 5 blocks around the mob. This enchantment is only found in the form of enchanting books found commonly in the nether fortress bridges.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Flame</summary>

This enchantment is unchanged from the base game, and goes up to two levels, lasting longer the higher level you have. This enchantment is found in the enchantment tables, random loot and villager trades.

</details>

## Special Bow Enchantments
This tier of enchantments is one of the new ones, it adds 3 enchantments, balooner, poison arrow and frozen arrow.


<details>
<summary>Balooner</summary>

### Balooner
this enchantment sends the shot enemy flying with levetaion 12 on hit. This enchantment has 3 levels, going from 0.5 seconds of levetation to 1 second, giving the mobs a great view, and a deal of damage. This enchantment is found on random loot, in the enchanting table and with villager trades.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Poison Arrow</summary>

### Poison Arrow
This enchantment gives the mob you hit poison for 5 seconds, it goes up to level 2, giving poison 2-3 (depending on level) On hit. This enchantment is found in the jungle temple chests.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Frozen Arrow</summary>

### Frozen Arrow
This enchantment freezes the mob you hit with the bow, allowing for you to easily hit it agian. There are two levels to this enchantment and with each level, you get one second of freezing, getting 2 seconds at the max level. This enchantment is found in the chest in the basement of the igloo.

</details>

</details>


# Sword Enchantments

<details>
<summary>Sword Enchantments</summary>

## Sword Enchanting Overview
There are some enchantments here to do with melee weapons, all are directly compatible on the swords, and are compatible to axes through books, except heavy hitter, swift strike and reach, which are directly compatible on axes.

## Primary Sword Enchantments
This is where you find the main two enchants of the pack, Swift Strike and Heavy Hitter. 

<details>
<summary>Swift Strike</summary>

### Swift Strike 
increases your attack speed by 1 per level, but decreases your damage by 0.5 per level, and having a max level of 6, means that you can get a weapon up to 2.2 attack speed at the cost of -3 damage. This enchantment is found in the enchanting table, and in various loot including villager trades.

</details>


<details>
<summary>Heavy Hitter</summary>

### Heavy Hitter
Increases your attack damage by 1.15 at level 1 and an extra .75 damage every level above it, but at the cost of lower attack speed, losing 1 attack speed per level. This enchantment can go up to the level of 6, meaning that at its max, it will give you 4.9 extra damage at the cost of having 6 slower attack speed. This enchantment is found in the enchanting table, and in various loot including villager trades.

</details>


## Secondary Sword Enchantments
Here you will find some general damage type enchantments, all of the slayer types will be here. There are 2 new enchantments here, ender and nether slayer, alongside smite.

<details>
<summary>Undead Slayer/Smite</summary>

### Undead Slayer/Smite
This enchantment is already in the game and remains unedited as of now, other than the fact that it is exlusive to the other secondary weapons, it does 2.5 extra damage per level to undead mobs, and goes up to level 5, meaning it does 12.5 extra damage to undead mobs at level 5. This enchantment is found in the enchanting table, and in various loot including villager trades.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Nether Slayer</summary>
  
### Nether Slayer
Nether slayer does more damage to mobs from the nether or if you are in the nether, it does 3 extra damage per level and goes up to level 5, doing 15 damage to mobs in or from the nether at its max echanting level. This enchantment is found in the enchanting table, and in various loot including villager trades. It is also found in ruined portals and nether fortresses.

</details>


<details>
<summary>Ender Slayer</summary>

### Ender Slayer
Ender slayer is just like nether slayer, doing more damage to mobs from the end  more damage if you are in the end, it does 3 extra damage per level up to 5, doing a maximum damage of 15 if you are in the end, or attacking mobs from the end. This enchantment is found in the enchanting table, and in various loot including villager trades. It is also found in stronghold libraries.

</details>


## Tertiary Sword Enchantments
Here you will find more specialised damage enchantments, doing damage to a few groups of mobs, also known as the "banes".

<details>
<summary>Illager's Bane</summary>

### Illager's Bane
This does an extra 2.5 damage per level to illagers and raiders, at its max enchantment level, 5, it does 12.5 extra damage to raiders. This enchantment is found in the enchanting table, and in various loot including villager trades, it is also found in pillager outposts.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Boss' Bane</summary>

### Boss' Bane
Dealing double the damage of the rest of the tertiary enchantments, at 5 damage per level, Boss' Bane can do some serious work if you fight a lot of bosses, doing 25 extra damage at max level to bosses. This enchantment is found in the enchanting table, and in various loot including villager trades.

</details>


<details>
<summary>Bane of Arthropods</summary>

### Bane Of Arthropods
Although I tried to make this enchantment more useful than it is in the base game, it is such a neiche enchantment, doing more damage to bugs, at 2.5 per level and a max of 12.5 extra damage, it is still quite useless. This enchantment is found in the enchanting table, and in various loot including villager trades.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Cubism</summary>

### Cubism (Yes, I know it doesn't have bane in it)
This enchantmnet came from the inspiring of hypixel skyblock, it does more damage to creepers, slimes, magma cubes and ghasts, doing 2.5 damage per level, at a max of 12.5 damage. This enchantment is found in the enchanting table, and in various loot including villager trades.

</details>


## Special Sword Enchantments
Here, you will find many different types of enchants, from damage to health to freezing an enemy in place, this is the most interesting enchantment type out of them all.

<details>
<summary>Lifesteal</summary>

### Lifesteal
Lifesteal is a healing enchantment reviving 2 hearts by a chance when you hit a mob. This enchantment starts at a 10% chance and increases by 5% every level, up to 25% at level 4. This enchantment is found in the chests of the ancient cities.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Wither Coat</summary>

### Wither Coat
This enchant gives the wither effect on hit, damaging the enemy, it does more damage than fire aspect, lasting from 5-7.5 seconds depending what level. This enchantment only goes up to level 2, and it lasts for 7.5 seconds at this level. This enchantment is found in mineshafts and nether fortesses as of the Definitive update v1.1.


</details>

<details>
<summary>Freeze</summary>

### Freeze
This enchant gives the hit entity slowness 10 effect, completely freezing them for 2-3 seconds on hit, and this enchantment only has one level. This enchantment is only found in the lower level of the igloos.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Fire Aspect</summary>

### Fire Aspect
This enchantment is unedited, and is left the same as it was. This enchantment is found in the enchanting table, and in various loot including villager trades.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Poison Tipped</summary>

### Poison Tipped
This enchant is quite confusing, as it does damage to some mobs and not others, as they are poison resistant. It is quite balanced, as no matter what, it can't kill the mobs, it brings them down to half a heart using poison, and then you can make the final strike, works well with swift strike. This enchantment is only found in the chests of the jungle temples.

</details>


## "Other" Sword Enchantments
This is just a misclanious part where there are two enchants, the other exlusivity rules do not apply to these two, and they are exlusive to different things, it says in their description.

<details>
<summary>Anti Knockback</summary>

### Anti Knockback
This enchantment is quite unreliable from my experience, but it hits the mobs back less than it does normally, and goes up to 2 levels. Its only exlusive enchantment is knockback. This enchantment is found in the enchanting table, and in various loot including villager trades.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reach</summary>

### Reach
This enchant allows you to reach an extra 2 blocks at its max level of 3, but it has the downside of the fact that it attacks slower by 2 attack speed, and is exlusive to sweeping edge. This enchantment is found in the enchanting table, and in various loot including villager trades.

</details>

</details>

# Axe Enchantments (Definitive version 2+)


<details>
<summary>Axe Enchantments</summary>

There are 4 axe enchantments (as of definitive v2), each having their own upsides and downsides, 
<details>
<summary>Critical Strike</summary>
Does more damage on critical hits, dealing more damage per level, going up to level 4, dealing an extra 2 damage, and 1.5 damage above the first level upon critting. It is incompatible with Shockwave, and charge, and its found when enchanting, and on random loot.


</details>

<details>
<summary>Rampage</summary>
Gives strength, and speed on hit, with increasing length according to the level, letting you easily kill many mobs, it is incompatible with critical strike. It is found in the Enchanting, and on random loot.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Charge</summary>
Does increasing damage that scales with your speed, going up to level 5, dealing 2.25x normal damage upon sprinting, and on the floor. This can easily kill many mobs, it is incompatible with shockwave, rampage, and Critical strike. Charge is found in enchanting, and random loot.

</details>
<details>
  
<summary>Shockwave</summary>
Unleashes upon critical strike, a deadly shockwave forms, dealing high amounts of damage, scaling with the level, up to level 3, at the cost of reduced attack rate, and destroying items on the floor. Shockwave is incompatible with Critical strike, Charge, and Heavy hitter. Works best with swift strike and rampage, and is found as a rare drop in trial vaults and ominous trial vaults. (one funny thing with this enchantment is that if the mob doesn't die when hit, other mobs will just kill them)


</details>

</details>

# Elytra Enchantments (definitive version 2+)

<details>
<summary>Elytra Enchantments</summary>
Provides many options for your new set of wings, giving small boosts to parts of flying.

<details>
<summary>Absorbing Wings</summary>
Gives absorption upon flying, protecting you from taking damage, taking 2-4 hearts of damage (depending on level) upon impact away from you, it is found in end cities, and is incompatible with reinforced wings.


</details>

<details>
<summary>Graceful Landing</summary>
This is a simple enchantment with one level, it prevents you from taking any fall damage when wearing the elytra, but at the cost of slower gliding speeds, it is also found in end city loot.


</details>

<details>
<summary>Protective Wings</summary>
Gives you one armor point per level, going up to level 5, replacing the armor that you would normally have with a chestplate, it is found in ancient cities, it is incompatible with absorbing wings.


</details>

</details>



## Other Changes
I have made some other changes to some of the enchantments, in order to make them more useable, or better.

<details>
<summary>Frost Walker</summary>
Frost Walker goes up to level 3, meaning you can sprint-Jump on water (yay)

</details>


<details>
<summary>Looting</summary>
Looting now works on Axes aswell as swords for easier acess to goods.

</details>


<details>
<summary>Quick Charge</summary>
Quick Charge goes up to level 5, allowing for some quick reloads, and making the Crossbow a more viable weapon in many situations.

</details>


<details>
<summary>Piercing</summary>
Piercing now works on normal bows.

</details>


<details>
<summary>Infinity</summary>
Infinity works on Crossbows, making them more feasable as a quick shooting bow with quick charge that does less damage than a bow, as it doesn't have power.

</details>

title: TWISB-Exploration
description: Exploration, the way it should be! This mod adds an Atlas item to contain all your maps, and makes compasses more useful.
body:
## Summary ##
Noticed how many people play with minimap mods, or often use the F3 screen for coordinates even though the vanilla game has maps and compasses? Thats because those items are not that usefull in vanilla. This mod adds an Atlas item to keep your maps tidy and buffs compasses.

I created this mod to improve Minecraft exploration while keeping it as close to Vanilla as possible. The goal is to take what is already in the game and make it actually useful (Mojang, if you read this, I would love if you added these changes to the game).


## The Atlas ##
The Atlas is a new item which can contain filled maps and shows the closest one to your current position. Here is the recipe:

![Crafting recipe for the Atlas](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/3ed2bb738f849106f8a34f37915f820274bbacb7.png)

It works like a bundle: select it and click on map items to place them in the Atlas. You can alternatively select the map and click it into the Atlas instead. To extract maps right click the Atlas onto an empty slot or right click the Atlas without any item selected.

Only maps of the same scale and dimension can be placed in an Atlas. For example, if the Atlas contain maps from the overworld it will not take maps from the nether.

If the Atlas contains a map, when you hold it, it will show the one closest to your location. 

If you right click while having empty maps in your inventory and the current location does not have a map in the Atlas, a new map will be made and added to the Atlas. If a new map made this way needs to be scaled (because other maps in the Atlas are scaled) paper will be required: one paper is used for each scale-up required.

## Compass buff ##
Having an compass in your inventory will show coordinates and faced direction (N/E/S/W).

The F3 screen does not show coordinates unless you're in creative mode (from mod version 0.1.4) or cheats are enabled (before mod version 0.1.3) giving you an actual reason to have a compass.

## Known bugs ##
For mod versions before 0.1.4 due to a vanilla Minecraft bug (afaik) you are able to place a map from the wrong dimension into an Atlas after reloading the game. Avoid doing that or it gets confusing.

## Check out my other mods ##
[TWISB-Enchanting](https://modrinth.com/mod/twisb-enchanting) Allows selecting enchantments in a vanilla-friendly way that promotes exploration. It also buffs anvils.

[TWISB-Combat](https://modrinth.com/mod/twisb-combat) Tweaks health regeneration, potions and tridents to make combat more interesting.

title: tpagui
description: A simple plugin that provides GUI functionality for TPA, supporting chest menus and Bedrock edition forms.
body:
# TpaGui

A simple plugin that provides GUI functionality for TPA, supporting chest menus and Bedrock Edition forms.

## Features

### Java Edition
- Chest menu interface
- Displays skulls of all online players
- Left-click to request teleportation to a player
- Right-click to request a player to teleport to you
- Supports multi-page display
- Previous/Next page buttons

### Bedrock Edition
- Dropdown form interface
- Player selection dropdown menu
- Teleport method toggle switch
- Automatically identifies Bedrock Edition players
- Teleport request popup
  - Shows requester's name
  - Shows teleport direction
  - Accept/Decline buttons
  - Closing the window automatically declines the request

### Common Features
- Supports customizing all message texts
- Supports color codes
- Allows viewing the list of online players from the console without relying on other plugins
